definition_zh: 伪证；伪证罪；虚假宣誓；背信
definition_en: the crime of telling a lie after swearing an oath to tell the truth, or such a false statement itself
core_image: 一手按在圣书上宣誓，嘴上说出的却是假话
scene: 法庭里证人举起手宣誓，却刻意说出与事实相反的证词。The witness took the oath, then told a deliberate lie, and later faced a charge of perjury.
sceneCN: 这里 perjury 是「伪证」（第 1 个义项：宣誓后作虚假陈述）；句意：证人宣誓之后故意撒谎，后来被控伪证。

derivatives.zh: 作伪证；使发假誓
作伪证的人
作过伪证的；发过假誓的
伪证的；处心积虑作假的

senses.title: A false statement under oath
senses.definition: a lie told while giving evidence on oath in a court or other legal hearing
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭或其他法律听证中宣誓作证时说的假话
senses.example: She was charged with perjury after the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判结束后她因伪证罪被起诉。
senses.why: The Latin root iurare means to swear, and the prefix per- carries the idea of ruin or perversion, so perjury is an oath turned into a lie.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 iurare 意为「宣誓」，前缀 per- 带「毁坏、颠倒」的意味，所以伪证就是被歪曲成谎言的誓言。

senses.title: The offence of lying on oath
senses.definition: the crime of knowingly making a false statement after swearing to tell the truth
senses.definitionCN: 明知虚假却在发誓说真话之后仍作虚假陈述的罪名
senses.example: The former minister was jailed for perjury.
senses.exampleCN: 那位前部长因伪证罪入狱。
senses.why: Once law turns the act into a named offence, the word names the crime itself, not only the words spoken.
senses.whyCN: 当法律把这种行为定为有名称的罪名后，这个词就指罪名本身，而不只是说出的假话。

senses.title: A false sworn declaration in writing
senses.definition: a false statement made in a sworn affidavit or a written declaration given under oath
senses.definitionCN: 在宣誓书或宣誓后作出的书面声明中写下的虚假陈述
senses.example: The court found that he had committed perjury in his affidavit.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定他在宣誓书中作了虚假陈述。
senses.why: The oath can be taken on paper as well as in the witness box, so the same act extends to sworn written statements.
senses.whyCN: 宣誓既可在证人席上作出，也可在纸上作出，因此同一种行为也延伸到宣誓后的书面陈述。

senses.title: Betraying a solemn promise
senses.definition: the breaking of a solemn promise or vow that has been made with an oath
senses.definitionCN: 违背曾以誓言形式作出的庄严承诺或誓愿
senses.example: To abandon his allies at that moment would have been a kind of moral perjury.
senses.exampleCN: 在那一刻抛弃盟友，无异于一种道德上的背信。
senses.why: A vow is an oath in everyday life, so breaking a sworn promise takes on the image of swearing falsely.
senses.whyCN: 誓愿在日常生活中就是一种誓言，因此违背宣过誓的承诺也带有虚假宣誓的意象。

senses.title: Falseness in written testimony
senses.definition: the state of sworn testimony or a sworn document being knowingly false
senses.definitionCN: 宣誓证词或宣誓文件被故意写成虚假内容的状态
senses.example: The defence argued that the whole record was riddled with perjury.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方主张整份记录充斥着失实的宣誓陈述。
senses.why: Judges and lawyers often speak of the condition of being false rather than of a single act, which gives this abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 法官与律师常说的不是某一次行为，而是「处于虚假状态」，由此产生这个抽象义项。

intro.en: Perjury comes from Latin periurium, a false oath, built from iurare, to swear, with the prefix per- meaning to ruin or pervert.
intro.cn: perjury 来自拉丁语 periurium（假誓），由 iurare（宣誓）加前缀 per-（毁坏、颠倒）构成。

items.en: Iurare means to swear an oath, and ius means law or right.
items.cn: iurare 意为宣誓，ius 意为法律或权利。

items.en: The prefix per- adds the sense of ruin or perversion, giving periurare, to swear falsely.
items.cn: 前缀 per- 赋予「毁坏、颠倒」之意，构成 periurare，意为发假誓。

items.en: Periurium is the noun for a false oath.
items.cn: periurium 是表示「假誓」的名词。

items.en: Perjurie carries the word into French law and speech.
items.cn: perjurie 把该词带入法语的法律与口语。

items.en: Perjurie appears in English with both the act and the crime.
items.cn: 中古英语 perjurie 同时表示作假行为与罪名。

items.en: Modern law fixes perjury as a named offence.
items.cn: 现代法律把伪证固定为一个有名称的罪名。

note.en: Perjury belongs to a small family of oath words: perjure, perjurer, perjured, and the general word for lying under oath.
note.cn: perjury 属于一个小型的「宣誓」词族：perjure、perjurer、perjured，以及表示「宣誓后撒谎」的通用词。

entries.definition: to make oneself guilty of perjury

having sworn falsely
saying things that are not true

normalIntro.en: Perjury is an oath with a lie hidden inside: the words of swearing and the lie share one breath.
normalIntro.cn: perjury 是藏在誓言里的谎言：宣誓的话与假话在同一口气里说出。

normal.en: The Latin iurare means to swear, so every perjury word carries an oath.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 iurare 意为宣誓，因此 perjury 的一切词形都带着誓言。

normal.en: To commit perjury is to lie after swearing to tell the truth.
normal.cn: commit perjury 就是在发誓说真话之后又撒谎。

normal.en: A perjury charge is the formal accusation of lying under oath.
normal.cn: a perjury charge 就是对宣誓后撒谎的正式指控。

normal.en: A perjurer is the person; perjure is the verb; perjured describes the false oath.
normal.cn: perjurer 是人，perjure 是动词，perjured 形容虚假的誓言。

normal.en: Compare lying: lying is any untruth, perjury is lying on oath in a legal setting.
normal.cn: 对比 lying：lying 泛指说假话，perjury 特指在法律场合宣誓后撒谎。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand and a Bible, with a lie slipping out between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在圣书上，假话从誓言之间溜了出来。

abstract.en: Think of a signature on a sworn statement that is deliberately false.
abstract.cn: 想象在一份宣誓声明上故意签下不实之词。

abstract.en: Imagine a broken promise still carrying the weight of a sworn vow.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被打破的承诺仍然背着誓言的重量。

examples.en: The witness was accused of perjury after contradicting his earlier statement.
examples.cn: 证人因与先前陈述矛盾而被控作伪证。

examples.en: Perjury is treated as a serious offence against the administration of justice.
examples.cn: 伪证被视为严重妨害司法的罪行。

examples.en: The company insisted that its earlier memo contained no perjury.
examples.cn: 公司坚称先前的备忘录里没有宣誓后的虚假陈述。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡姐瑞」——在法庭上把誓言当成坡道往下滑，滑出一堆假话；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 iurare（宣誓）+ 前缀 per-（毁坏、颠倒）→ periurium（假誓）→ 古法语 perjurie → 英语 perjury，核心义「把誓言变成谎言」。

sensesIntro.en: Perjury first names the false statement under oath, then the crime, then a false sworn statement in writing, then a broken vow, and finally the state of being false.
sensesIntro.cn: perjury 先指宣誓后的虚假陈述，再指罪名，然后是书面虚假宣誓陈述，接着是违背誓约，最后指「处于虚假」的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a holy book while a lie leaves the mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：手按圣书，嘴里却说出假话。

branches.en: The false statement under oath is the everyday legal core.
branches.cn: 宣誓后的虚假陈述是最日常的法律核心义。

branches.en: The named offence turns the act into a crime.
branches.cn: 有名称的罪名把这种行为转成犯罪。

branches.en: Sworn written statements repeat the act on paper.
branches.cn: 宣誓后的书面陈述把同一行为搬到纸上。

branches.en: A broken vow is the oath image extended to ordinary life.
branches.cn: 违背誓约是誓言意象向日常生活的延伸。

branches.en: The abstract sense names the condition of sworn falsehood.
branches.cn: 抽象义项指「宣誓内容处于虚假」的状态。

definition_zh: 渗透；弥漫；贯穿；透过
definition_en: to spread through every part of something, or to pass slowly through a material or barrier
core_image: 雾气从缝隙钻进来，慢慢填满整间屋子
scene: 清晨的咖啡香从厨房飘出，一点一点钻进客厅。A warm smell of freshly baked bread permeated every corner of the flat by noon.
sceneCN: 这里 permeate 是「弥漫、贯穿」（第 2 个义项：成为影响、渗入每一部分）；句意：到中午时，新烤面包的暖香弥漫了公寓的每个角落。

derivatives.zh: 可渗透的；可透过的
渗透性；可渗透性
不可渗透的
渗透；弥漫

senses.title: To spread through every part
senses.definition: to spread gradually into every part of something porous or open
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐进入多孔或开放之物的每一个部分
senses.example: Steam permeated the whole room within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 几分钟内蒸汽就弥漫了整个房间。
senses.why: The Latin per- means through and meare means to pass, so the word pictures liquid or vapour passing through every pore.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀 per- 意为「穿过」，meare 意为「经过」，所以这个词描绘液体或气体穿过每一个孔隙。

senses.title: To become part of everything
senses.definition: to become an influence felt in every part of a situation, group, or atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 成为一种影响，渗入某种情境、群体或氛围的每一部分
senses.example: A sense of celebration permeated the whole school.
senses.exampleCN: 庆祝的气氛感染了整个学校。
senses.why: What spreads through a physical medium can also spread through a mood or a group, so the image moves from matter to feeling.
senses.whyCN: 能从物中渗透的东西也能渗透进情绪或群体，因此意象从物质转向感受。

senses.title: To soak into and through
senses.definition: to pass slowly into and through a material such as cloth, soil, or skin
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢地进入并穿过布料、土壤或皮肤等材料
senses.example: Rainwater had permeated the cloth and left it damp.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水渗进了布料，把它弄得潮湿。
senses.why: Slow soaking is the most physical version of the through-passing image, close to the smell and dampness of everyday things.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢浸透是「穿过」意象里最具体的一种，贴近日常物品的气息与潮湿。

senses.title: To pass through a barrier
senses.definition: to move through a membrane, filter, or other barrier and reach the space beyond
senses.definitionCN: 穿过薄膜、滤层或其他屏障并进入另一侧的空间
senses.example: Only small molecules can permeate the membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 只有小分子能够透过这层薄膜。
senses.why: Science uses the word for passage across a barrier, so the through-motion becomes a measurable transfer.
senses.whyCN: 科学用法指越过屏障的通过，于是「穿过」变成了可测量的转移。

senses.title: To be understood or felt widely
senses.definition: to be recognized or felt widely by many people in an organization or society
senses.definitionCN: 在一个组织或社会中被许多人普遍认同或感受到
senses.example: The idea of remote work has permeated the business world.
senses.exampleCN: 远程办公的理念已经渗入了商界。
senses.why: When a thought passes through a large group, it feels like vapour filling a building, which gives this wide-spread sense.
senses.whyCN: 当一种想法在庞大的群体中穿行，就像气体充满整栋楼，由此产生这种广泛传播的义项。

intro.en: Permeate comes from Latin permeare, to pass through, built from per-, through, and meare, to pass or go.
intro.cn: permeate 来自拉丁语 permeare（穿过），由 per-（穿过）与 meare（经过）构成。

items.en: Meare means to pass or go, the source of English meatus and of permeate itself.
items.cn: meare 意为经过或行进，是英语 meatus 与 permeate 的来源。

items.en: Permeare adds the prefix per- to give passing through.
items.cn: permeare 加上前缀 per-，表示「穿过」。

items.en: Permeabilis describes something that can be passed through.
items.cn: permeabilis 描述可被穿过的物体。

items.en: The verb enters English scientific writing as a word for passage through a body.
items.cn: 该动词进入英语科学写作，表示穿过物体。

items.en: Modern usage extends the through-passing to ideas, moods, and systems.
items.cn: 现代英语把「穿过」延伸到思想、情绪与制度。

note.en: Permeate shares the Latin through-passing root with permeable and impermeable, and sits near leakage and spread words.
note.cn: permeate 与 permeable、impermeable 共享拉丁语「穿过」词根，并与表示渗漏、扩散的词相邻。

entries.definition: allowing liquid or gas to pass through
not allowing passage through
the quality of letting things pass through
the process of spreading through
to make something completely wet by letting liquid enter
to fill something completely so that no more can enter
to flow slowly through small openings

normalIntro.en: Permeate is water finding every tiny hole in cloth: nothing stays dry, everything gets through.
normalIntro.cn: permeate 就是水找到了布上的每一个小孔：没有一处保持干燥，什么都穿得过去。

normal.en: Per- means through, so permeate is about going through and beyond.
normal.cn: per- 表示穿过，所以 permeate 讲的是穿过并遍布。

normal.en: Smells and sounds permeate the air; liquids permeate cloth.
normal.cn: 气味和声音弥漫在空气中，液体浸透布料。

normal.en: A membrane that lets molecules pass is permeable; one that blocks them is impermeable.
normal.cn: 让分子通过的薄膜是可渗透的，阻断分子的则是不可渗透的。

normal.en: The noun form is permeation, the quality form is permeability.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 permeation，性质名词是 permeability。

normal.en: Compare seep: seep is a small slow leak, permeate is spreading through every part.
normal.cn: 对比 seep：seep 是小而慢的渗漏，permeate 则是渗入每一部分。

abstract.en: Picture mist seeping under a door and filling every room of a house.
abstract.cn: 想象雾从门下钻入，填满房子的每个房间。

abstract.en: Think of a catchy song playing in every corner of a festival.
abstract.cn: 想象一首上口的歌在节日的每个角落回荡。

abstract.en: Imagine rainwater sinking into soil until the whole garden turns dark and damp.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水渗进泥土，直到整座花园都变得深色而潮湿。

examples.en: The smell of coffee permeated the small cafe.
examples.cn: 咖啡香弥漫了整个小咖啡馆。

examples.en: A spirit of cooperation permeated the negotiations.
examples.cn: 合作精神贯穿了整个谈判。

examples.en: Water permeated the soil after several days of rain.
examples.cn: 连续几天的降雨后，水渗进了土壤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼米·特」——一盆水泼进米里，水穿透每一粒米的缝隙；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（穿过）+ meare（经过）→ permeare（穿过）→ 英语 permeate，核心义「从孔隙中穿过并遍布」。

sensesIntro.en: Permeate starts with physical spreading into every part, then mood or influence, then slow soaking, then passing a barrier, and finally wide-spread understanding.
sensesIntro.cn: permeate 先从物理上渗入每一部分，再到情绪或影响，然后是缓慢浸透、穿越屏障，最后是被广泛理解。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: mist seeping in and filling every room.
core.cn: 核心意象：雾气渗进来，填满每个房间。

branches.en: Spreading into every part is the physical core.
branches.cn: 渗入每一部分是物理核心义。

branches.en: Mood and influence are the atmosphere sense.
branches.cn: 情绪与影响是氛围义项。

branches.en: Slow soaking is the absorption sense.
branches.cn: 缓慢浸透是吸收义项。

branches.en: Passing a barrier is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 穿越屏障是技术义项。

branches.en: Wide-spread understanding crosses into social life.
branches.cn: 被广泛理解跨越到社会生活层面。

items.example: The suffix -able forms permeable.

definition_zh: 允许的；可准许的；可接受的；合规的
definition_en: allowed by a rule, law, or authority, or acceptable within reason
core_image: 一扇门前有人点头放行，门内还写着一条上限
scene: 图书馆入口贴着告示，馆内只许轻声交谈。Quiet conversation is permissible in the reading room, but phone calls are not.
sceneCN: 这里 permissible 是「被允许的」（第 1 个义项：规则允许、非被禁止的）；句意：阅览室里允许轻声交谈，但不许打电话。

pos.zh: 允许的；可准许的；可接受的

derivatives.zh: 许可；允许
允许；许可证
宽容的；放任的
不允许的；不可接受的

senses.title: Allowed by rules
senses.definition: allowed by a law, rule, or authority rather than forbidden
senses.definitionCN: 由法律、规则或权威允许，而非被禁止的
senses.example: Personal phone calls are not permissible during the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试期间不允许打私人电话。
senses.why: The Latin prefix per- here means through after all, and mittere means to let go, so permission is letting something pass.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀 per- 在这里意为「通过」，mittere 意为「放走」，所以许可就是让某事通过。

senses.title: Acceptable in a judgement
senses.definition: acceptable or allowable when judged by fairness, reason, or standards of taste
senses.definitionCN: 按公平、理性或品味标准衡量时可以接受、说得过去的
senses.example: Some error is permissible in a first draft.
senses.exampleCN: 初稿里出现一些错误是可以接受的。
senses.why: Rules are not the only measure; a permissible thing can also be one that fair judgement lets through.
senses.whyCN: 规则并非唯一标准，可允许之事也可以是被公平判断放行的事情。

senses.title: Allowed morally or legally
senses.titleCN: 在道德或法律上许可的
senses.definition: permitted by moral principles or by a formal legal system
senses.definitionCN: 得到道德原则或正式法律体系许可的
senses.example: The court asked whether such a search was constitutionally permissible.
senses.exampleCN: 法院追问这样的搜查在宪法上是否被允许。
senses.why: This sense stresses the authority behind the permission: it is not merely handy but sanctioned by law or ethics.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项强调许可背后的权威：不只是方便，而是经法律或伦理认可。

senses.title: Able to be permitted or admitted
senses.definition: capable of being granted permission or admitted as evidence or argument
senses.definitionCN: 有资格获得许可、或可作为证据与陈述被接纳的
senses.example: Only admissible evidence is permissible in closing argument.
senses.exampleCN: 只有可采纳的证据才能在结案陈词中使用。
senses.why: In court language, a permissible item is one the rules admit, which borrows the passing-through image of admission.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭用语中，permissible 指规则允许接纳之物，借用了「通过准入」的意象。

senses.title: Allowable within limits
senses.definition: within the limits set by an agreement, policy, or standard, and no further
senses.definitionCN: 在协议、政策或标准所设限度之内、不可再多的
senses.example: The museum allows a permissible noise level of fifty decibels.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆允许的噪音水平是五十分贝。
senses.why: When a standard names an upper limit, the word describes anything that stays inside that limit.
senses.whyCN: 当标准给出上限，这个词就描述仍处在该限度之内的事物。

intro.en: Permissible comes from Latin permittere, to let through, from per-, through, and mittere, to send or let go.
intro.cn: permissible 来自拉丁语 permittere（放行），由 per-（穿过）与 mittere（送出、放走）构成。

items.en: Mittere means to send or let go.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出或放走。

items.en: Permittere means to let through or allow.
items.cn: permittere 意为放行、允许。

items.en: Permissibilis describes something that can be allowed.
items.cn: permissibilis 描述可被允许的事物。

items.en: Permettre and permis carry the permission word into French.
items.cn: permettre 与 permis 把「许可」词带入法语。

items.en: Permission and permit appear in English first, then the adjective.
items.cn: 英语先出现 permission 与 permit，其后才有该形容词。

items.en: Permissible settles into legal and technical writing.
items.cn: permissible 逐渐固定用于法律与技术写作。

note.en: Permissible is the adjective of permit and permission, and sits close to allowable, acceptable, and permitted.
note.cn: permissible 是 permit 与 permission 的形容词形式，与 allowable、acceptable、permitted 相邻。

entries.definition: the act of allowing something
to allow something to happen
allowing much freedom
not allowed
accepted as within the rules
good enough to be agreed to
allowed by law or fair reason

normalIntro.en: Permissible carries the image of a gatekeeper nodding: something is allowed to pass the gate, but only within limits.
normalIntro.cn: permissible 带着守门人点头放行的意象：某物可以通过这道门，但只限在规定之内。

normal.en: Permission is the noun, permit is the verb, permissible is the adjective of allowing.
normal.cn: permission 是名词，permit 是动词，permissible 表示被允许的。

normal.en: Permissible under the law means the law allows it.
normal.cn: permissible under the law 意为法律允许它。

normal.en: Impermissible is the negative form, formed with the prefix im-.
normal.cn: impermissible 是否定形式，由前缀 im- 构成。

normal.en: A permissible level is the highest amount the rules allow.
normal.cn: a permissible level 就是规则允许的最高量。

normal.en: Compare permissive: permissive describes a person or policy that allows much, permissible describes what is allowed.
normal.cn: 对比 permissive：permissive 形容宽容的人或政策，permissible 形容被允许的事物。

abstract.en: Picture a guard raising one hand to let a car through a checkpoint.
abstract.cn: 想象卫兵抬手示意一辆车通过检查站。

abstract.en: Think of a ruler laid along a sheet of paper; anything under the line is fine.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺贴着纸面，线以下的都算合格。

abstract.en: Imagine a judge nodding at a lawyer and saying the question may stand.
abstract.cn: 想象法官向律师点头，说这个问题可以保留。

examples.en: Smoking is not permissible anywhere inside the building.
examples.cn: 大楼内任何地方都不允许吸烟。

examples.en: The agreement sets a permissible limit on noise at night.
examples.cn: 协议规定了夜间噪音的可允许上限。

examples.en: It is permissible to bring a calculator into the exam.
examples.cn: 考试时可以携带计算器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派市宝」——只有被批准派到市面上的宝贝才是被允许的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（穿过）+ mittere（送出、放走）→ permittere（放行、允许）→ permissibilis → 英语 permissible，核心义「被放行、被允许」。

sensesIntro.en: Permissible begins with what rules allow, then what reason accepts, then moral or legal sanction, then what courts admit, and finally what stays inside a limit.
sensesIntro.cn: permissible 先从规则允许之物说起，再到理性可接受之物，然后是道德与法律认可、法庭可采纳，最后是仍在限度之内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gatekeeper nods and something passes the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：守门人点头，某物通过大门。

branches.en: What rules allow is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 规则允许之物是日常义项。

branches.en: What reason accepts is the judgement sense.
branches.cn: 理性可接受是判断义项。

branches.en: Moral and legal sanction back the permission.
branches.cn: 道德与法律给许可作后盾。

branches.en: What courts admit is the procedural sense.
branches.cn: 法庭可采纳是程序义项。

branches.en: Anything inside the set limit counts as permissible.
branches.cn: 仍在规定限度内的事物都算被允许。

intro.en: Permissible is the adjective of the Latin verb permittere, with permission, permit, and permissive as its English family.
intro.cn: permissible 是拉丁语动词 permittere 的形容词形式，英语词族有 permission、permit 与 permissive。

latinIntro.en: Latin per- means through and mittere means to send or let go, so permittere means to let pass, and permissibilis means that which may be let pass.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 per- 意为穿过，mittere 意为送出或放走，因此 permittere 意为放行，permissibilis 意为可被放行的。

items.example: The prefix per- gives the sense of passing through.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 per- 给出「通过」的含义。

items.example: Mittere provides the allowing core.
items.exampleCN: mittere 提供「放行」的核心义。

items.example: Permittere is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: permittere 是直接来源。

items.example: Permissibilis becomes permissible in English.
items.exampleCN: permissibilis 在英语中变为 permissible。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms permissible.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ible 构成 permissible。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ssion forms permission.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ssion 构成 permission。

items.example: The prefix im- negates permissible.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 否定 permissible。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms permissive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 permissive。

items.example: Permit is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: permit 是简短的英语动词。

definition_zh: 排列；置换；换位；排列方式；（数学）置换
definition_en: a change in the order of a set of things, or one of the possible orders in which a set of things can be arranged
core_image: 一排椅子上的字母被两两交换位置，换出一种新的顺序
scene: 学生把课桌重新排过几次，每次上课的样子都不一样。After several permutations of the seating plan, the coordinator felt every arrangement had been tried.
sceneCN: 这里 permutation 是「排列方式、一种换法」（第 3 个义项：各种可能的排列结果之一）；句意：座位方案被排过好几种之后，协调人觉得每种排法都试过了。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 permutare 直接借入的动词，义为「置换；改变次序」
permutation 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「排列的；置换的」
permute 加 -able 构成，义为「可置换的；能改变次序的」

senses.title: The act of rearranging things
senses.definition: the act of changing the order or arrangement of a set of things
senses.definitionCN: 改变一组事物的顺序或摆放方式的行为
senses.example: The permutation of the lists took the clerk a whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 把几份名单重新排列花了职员一整个下午。
senses.why: Latin per- means thoroughly and mutare means to change, so the core act is changing the order through and through.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 per- 表示「彻底」，mutare 表示「改变」，所以核心动作是把顺序彻底换过一遍。

senses.title: A change in the order of things
senses.definition: a change in the way things are ordered or combined, often a variation of an earlier version
senses.definitionCN: 事物排列或组合方式的改变，常指前一版本的变体
senses.example: The film is a permutation of the same old story.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影不过是同一个老故事的另一种变体。
senses.why: If the order has been changed, the result looks like a variation of the original, so the word widens to any new version.
senses.whyCN: 顺序既然被改动，结果就像原版的一个变体，于是词义扩展到「任何新版本、新变体」。

senses.title: One possible arrangement
senses.titleCN: 一种排列方式；排列结果
senses.definition: one of the possible orders in which a group of items can be arranged
senses.definitionCN: 一组事物所有可能顺序中的某一种
senses.example: With four items there are twenty-four permutations.
senses.exampleCN: 四个事物共有二十四种排列。
senses.why: The abstract act can be counted: each different order produced is a permutation in its own right.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的「换位动作」可以数出来：每一种排出来的不同顺序，本身就叫做一个排列。

senses.title: A substitution in a row
senses.definition: an act of exchanging the positions of two or more items, often as a substitution
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或多个项目的位置互相调换，常带有替换的意味
senses.example: A small permutation in the opening line changed the tone of the poem.
senses.exampleCN: 开头一行的小小换位改变了整首诗的语气。
senses.why: Swapping two positions is the smallest visible form of the core act, so the word names a plain exchange.
senses.whyCN: 互换两个位置是核心动作最小、最可见的形式，所以这个词也指平实的「对调、替换」。

senses.title: An ordered selection in mathematics
senses.definition: an arrangement of a set of items in a definite order, or the number of such arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 把一组元素按一定顺序排好，或这种排法的数目
senses.example: The students counted every permutation under the given rule.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们按给定规则数出所有的排列。
senses.why: Mathematics turns the everyday act into a precise object: the order matters, and every distinct order can be counted.
senses.whyCN: 数学把日常的换位变成精确的对象：顺序重要，而且每一种不同的顺序都可以被计数。

intro.en: Permutation comes from Latin permutare, to change completely, built from per-, thoroughly, and mutare, to change.
intro.cn: permutation 来自拉丁语 permutare（彻底改变），由 per-（彻底）与 mutare（改变）构成。

items.en: Mutare means to change or exchange.
items.cn: mutare 意为改变、交换。

items.en: Permutare adds the intensive per-: to change thoroughly or swap completely.
items.cn: permutare 加上加强语气的前缀 per-：彻底改变、完全交换。

items.en: The noun permutatio names an exchange or interchange.
items.cn: 名词 permutatio 指交换或互换。

items.en: Older French permutacion carries the noun onward.
items.cn: 古法语 permutacion 把这个名词带向英语。

items.en: English first uses permutation for a swapping or exchanging of matters.
items.cn: 英语最早用 permutation 表示事物的交换与调换。

items.en: Mathematics later fixes the word to ordered arrangements of a set.
items.cn: 后来数学把这个词固定为「集合的有序排列」。

note.en: Permutation shares the Latin root mutare with mutation, commute, and transmute, and sits near arrangement, in maths especially.
note.cn: permutation 与 mutation、commute、transmute 共享拉丁词根 mutare，含义上靠近 arrangement，尤其在数学语境里。

entries.definition: to change the order or arrangement of something
a change into a different form
entries.definitionCN: 变异；改变（同为拉丁语 mutare 词根）

entries.definition: to travel regularly to and from work
entries.definitionCN: 通勤；往返（词根本义为「交换、折换」）

entries.definition: the way things are placed or ordered
a thing that is slightly different from another of the same type
a set of items put together, in which order does not matter
entries.definitionCN: 组合；搭配（与「排列」相对，不计顺序）

normalIntro.en: Permutation is a thorough change of order: the pieces stay, the sequence turns.
normalIntro.cn: permutation 是彻底的换序：东西还是那些东西，次序却被翻了过来。

normal.en: Break it up as per + mutation: a change carried through.
normal.cn: 拆成 per 加 mutation：一次被彻底完成的改变。

normal.en: In maths, permutation and combination are a fixed pair: order counts in the first.
normal.cn: 数学里 permutation and combination 成对出现：前者讲究顺序。

normal.en: Every possible permutation means all the orders you could try.
normal.cn: every possible permutation 指所有能试的顺序。

normal.en: The verb permute is shorter and names the act itself.
normal.cn: 动词 permute 更短，直接表示「置换」这个动作。

normal.en: Compare combination: a combination ignores order, a permutation keeps it.
normal.cn: 对比 combination：组合不看顺序，排列看顺序。

abstract.en: Picture letters on chairs swapping seats one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象椅子上的字母一个接一个换座位。

abstract.en: Picture the same story retold with the chapters shuffled.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个故事把章节顺序打乱后重讲一遍。

abstract.en: Imagine four coloured blocks forming twenty-four distinct rows.
abstract.cn: 想象四块彩色积木排出二十四种不同的队列。

examples.en: The team tested several permutations of the design before choosing one.
examples.cn: 团队试了好几种设计排列方案才选定一种。

examples.en: Permutation is the branch of counting in which order matters.
examples.cn: 排列是讲究顺序的一类计数问题。

examples.en: A tiny permutation of the words made the sentence clearer.
examples.cn: 把词的位置稍稍换一下，句子就清楚了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「颇谬」——把东西的顺序改得颇为谬误，就是一通乱换位；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（彻底）+ mutare（改变）→ permutare（彻底改变、完全交换）→ permutatio（交换）→ 古法语 → 英语 permutation，核心义「把次序彻底换过」。

sensesIntro.en: Permutation starts with the act of reordering, moves to the change and its versions, and ends in the mathematical count of possible orders.
sensesIntro.cn: permutation 先指重新排序这个动作，再指变动与变体，最后落在数学上可数的各种可能顺序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: letters on a row of chairs swapping seats.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排椅子上的字母互相换座位。

branches.en: The act of reordering is the base sense.
branches.cn: 重新排序的动作是基础义项。

branches.en: A new order becomes a new version.
branches.cn: 新的次序变成新的版本。

branches.en: Each distinct order is one permutation.
branches.cn: 每一种不同的顺序就是一个排列。

branches.en: A swap of positions is a small permutation.
branches.cn: 位置的互换是小小的置换。

branches.en: Mathematics turns ordered arrangements into objects to count.
branches.cn: 数学把有序排法变成可计数的对象。

intro.en: Permutation is built from the Latin prefix per-, the root mutare, and the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: permutation 由拉丁语前缀 per-、词根 mutare 与名词词尾 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin per- strengthens the verb, and mutare supplies the idea of change.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 per- 加强动词语气，mutare 提供「改变」的核心概念。

items.example: The prefix per- adds force to the verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 per- 给动词加上「彻底」的力量。

items.example: Mutare is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: mutare 是整个词族的词根。

items.meaning: the act or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation turns the verb into an action noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 把动词变成动作名词。

items.example: Mutation keeps the bare root mutare.
items.exampleCN: mutation 直接保留词根 mutare。

items.example: Mutate is built straight on the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: mutate 直接建在拉丁语动词之上。

items.meaning: to exchange, now to travel regularly
items.example: Com- plus mutare gives an exchange.
items.exampleCN: com- 加 mutare 表示互相交换。

items.meaning: to change into a different substance
items.example: Trans- plus mutare gives change across forms.
items.exampleCN: trans- 加 mutare 表示跨越形态的改变。

items.example: Permute is the shorter verb of the same root.
items.exampleCN: permute 是同一词根的短动词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms permutable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 permutable。

items.example: The suffix -al forms permutational.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 permutational。

definition_zh: 犯；干（坏事）；实施（罪行）；做出（错误、玩笑等）
definition_en: to commit a crime, a wrong act, or a serious mistake
core_image: 一个人在暗处把罪行从头做到尾，最后一次收手
scene: 警方调取了近半年的案卷，想弄清这些案子究竟是谁干的。Inspectors believe a single group perpetrated the fraud across three cities.
sceneCN: 这里 perpetrate 是「实施、犯下」（第 1 个义项：犯下罪行等严重坏事）；句意：调查人员认为，同一个团伙在三个城市里实施了这起诈骗。

derivatives.zh: perpetrate 加施动后缀 -or 构成，义为「实施者；犯罪者」
perpetrate 加 -ion 构成，义为「实施；犯下（罪行）」

senses.title: To commit a crime or wrongdoing
senses.definition: to commit a crime, an outrage, or another seriously wrong act
senses.definitionCN: 犯下罪行、暴行等严重错误的行为
senses.example: The gang perpetrated a series of robberies along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这伙人在沿海一带犯下了一系列抢劫案。
senses.why: Latin per- means through and patrare means to carry out, so the word pictures an evil deed carried through to the end.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 per- 表示「贯穿到底」，patrare 表示「完成、办成」，所以这个词画的是一件恶事被一路做到底。

senses.title: To carry out an action, often badly
senses.definition: to do or carry out something, especially an action that turns out badly
senses.definitionCN: 做出或执行某事，尤指结果很糟的举动
senses.example: At the gala he perpetrated a joke that nobody found funny.
senses.exampleCN: 在晚会上他讲了一个谁都没觉得好笑的玩笑。
senses.why: Once a deed is pictured as something carried out, the verb can cover any boldly executed act, including a bad joke or a blunder.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把行为看成「被办成的事」，这个动词就能覆盖任何大胆做出的举动，包括糟糕的玩笑或蠢事。

intro.en: Perpetrate comes from Latin perpetrare, to carry out, from per-, through, and patrare, to bring about, probably related to pater, father.
intro.cn: perpetrate 来自拉丁语 perpetrare（完成、办成），由 per-（贯穿）与 patrare（促成、完成）构成，而 patrare 一般认为与 pater（父亲）有关。

items.en: Patrare means to carry out or accomplish, listed with meanings of a father bringing something about.
items.cn: patrare 意为完成、促成，古代注家还把它与父亲「成就、办妥」的意思相提并论。

items.en: Perpetrare adds per-: to carry a deed through to the end.
items.cn: perpetrare 加上 per-：把一件事一路做到底。

items.en: Late Latin later uses the verb chiefly for evil or criminal deeds.
items.cn: 后期的拉丁语渐渐把这个动词主要用于邪恶或犯罪的勾当。

items.en: English borrows perpetrate and keeps the flavour of a deed boldly done.
items.cn: 英语借入 perpetrate，保留了「大胆做成某事」的意味。

items.en: Modern usage narrows to crimes and wrongs, with ironic uses for silly acts.
items.cn: 现代用法收窄到罪行与坏事，也用于带讽刺意味的蠢事。

note.en: Perpetrate should not be confused with perpetual, which sounds close but means lasting forever, and it sits beside commit and carry out.
note.cn: perpetrate 易与拼写相近的 perpetual 混淆，后者意为「永久的」，两者词源不同；含义上它靠近 commit 与 carry out。

entries.definition: lasting for ever or seeming to never end
entries.definitionCN: 永久的；不停的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a person who commits a crime or a wrong act
to make something continue for a long time
entries.definitionCN: 使延续；使长存（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to do something illegal or wrong
to carry out a plan or an order
to make someone suffer something unpleasant

normalIntro.en: Perpetrate is the verb of deeds carried through: per-, through, plus patrare, to accomplish.
normalIntro.cn: perpetrate 是「把事做到底」的动词：per-（贯穿）加上 patrare（完成）。

normal.en: Break it up as per + petrate: a deed done all the way through.
normal.cn: 拆成 per 加 patrare：一件从头做到尾的事。

normal.en: The person is the perpetrator, the act is the perpetration.
normal.cn: 做这事的人叫 perpetrator，这个行为叫 perpetration。

normal.en: You perpetrate a crime or a fraud, not a meal or a nap.
normal.cn: 你 perpetrate 的是罪行或诈骗，不会用来说吃一顿饭或小睡。

normal.en: Keep it apart from perpetual: one is an act, the other a duration.
normal.cn: 和 perpetual 分清：一个是作出的行为，一个是持续的时间。

normal.en: Compare commit: commit is the everyday legal verb, perpetrate sounds heavier and formal.
normal.cn: 对比 commit：commit 是日常的法律动词，perpetrate 更沉重、更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling a lever all the way down in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中一只手把操纵杆一路拉到底。

abstract.en: Picture a mischief-maker grinning after finishing the whole prank.
abstract.cn: 想象恶作剧者把整套把戏做完后得意地笑。

abstract.en: Picture a path worn through pressed deep into the ground by repeated steps.
abstract.cn: 想象反复踩踏踩出的一条深深小径。

examples.en: Police are hunting the men who perpetrated the attack.
examples.cn: 警方正在追捕实施那次袭击的人。

examples.en: The same error was perpetrated by two successive editors.
examples.cn: 同样的错误前后两任编辑都犯过。

examples.en: The perpetrator was caught on camera.
examples.cn: 作案人被监控拍到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破皮踹他」——干了坏事还想踹人跑掉，正是「犯罪的所作所为」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（贯穿到底）+ patrare（完成、办成；一般与 pater 父亲有关）→ perpetrare（把事做完）→ 英语 perpetrate，核心义「把坏事一桩干到底」。

sensesIntro.en: Perpetrate has a heavy sense for serious crimes and a lighter, often ironic sense for actions like jokes and errors.
sensesIntro.cn: perpetrate 既指沉重地实施严重罪行，也指轻一点、常带讽刺地「做出」玩笑、错误这类举动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lever pulled all the way down.
core.cn: 核心意象：操纵杆被一路拉到底。

branches.en: A wrong act carried through becomes a crime.
branches.cn: 一件做到底的坏事就成了罪行。

branches.en: Any boldly executed act, such as a bad joke, fits the same frame.
branches.cn: 任何大胆办成的事，比如一个糟糕的玩笑，也都套得上同一框架。

branches.en: Both senses show a deed deliberately seen through.
branches.cn: 两个义项都体现「故意做成」的动作。

branches.en: The person behind the deed is the perpetrator.
branches.cn: 做出这件事的人就是 perpetrator。

branches.en: Formality and disapproval run through the whole word.
branches.cn: 正式与贬义贯穿整个词的用法。

intro.en: Perpetrate pairs the Latin prefix per- with the verb patrare and the English verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: perpetrate 由拉丁语前缀 per-、动词 patrare 与英语动词词尾 -ate 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin per- means through, and patrare means to carry out or accomplish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 per- 表示「贯穿」，patrare 表示「完成、办成」。

items.example: The prefix per- stresses doing something through.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 per- 强调把事贯穿做完。

items.example: Patrare supplies the idea of accomplishment.
items.exampleCN: patrare 提供「成就、办成」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ate turns the Latin stem into an English verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把拉丁词干变成英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -or forms perpetrator.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 perpetrator。

items.meaning: a person who commits a crime
items.example: Perpetrator names the person behind the deed.
items.exampleCN: perpetrator 指做出这件事的人。

items.meaning: the act or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms perpetration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 perpetration。

items.example: Perpetration names the act itself.
items.exampleCN: perpetration 指行为本身。

items.example: Patrare is traditionally linked with pater.
items.exampleCN: patrare 一般认为与 pater 有关。

items.example: Perpetual is built on petere, a different root.
items.exampleCN: perpetual 建在 petere 上，是另一个词根。

definition_zh: 永久的；永恒的；持续不断的；（植物）四季开花的
definition_en: continuing for ever, or seeming never to stop
core_image: 一枚环形的钟摆，一圈接一圈，始终不肯停下
scene: 那台老冰箱整夜嗡嗡作响，连墙都在跟着轻颤。A perpetual hum from the fridge kept the whole flat awake.
sceneCN: 这里 perpetual 是「持续不断的、没完没了的」（第 2 个义项：反复出现、似乎停不下来的）；句意：冰箱持续不断的嗡嗡声让整间公寓的人都没睡着。

derivatives.zh: perpetual 加副词尾 -ly 构成，义为「永远地；不停地」
perpetual 去掉形容词尾、改用动词形式，义为「使延续；使长存」
由拉丁语 perpetuitas 借入的抽象名词，义为「永恒；永久」

senses.title: Lasting for ever
senses.definition: lasting for ever or for an extremely long time
senses.definitionCN: 永远持续，或持续极长的时间
senses.example: They carved their names as a symbol of perpetual love.
senses.exampleCN: 他们刻下彼此的名字，作为永恒爱情的象征。
senses.why: Latin per- means through and petere means to seek or reach, so perpetual first pictures something that keeps going without end.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 per- 表示「贯穿」，petere 表示「追求、抵达」，所以 perpetual 最初画的是那种一直延续、没有尽头的东西。

senses.title: Never stopping
senses.titleCN: 持续不断的；没完没了的
senses.definition: repeated so often that it seems never to stop
senses.definitionCN: 反复出现到似乎永远停不下来
senses.example: Her perpetual complaints wear the whole team down.
senses.exampleCN: 她没完没了的抱怨把整个团队都拖垮了。
senses.why: When something does not end, it comes back again and again, so the word also means annoyingly constant.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然没有尽头，就会一次又一次地回来，于是这个词也带上「令人厌烦地不断」的意味。

senses.title: Flowering all year
senses.definition: used of a plant that flowers or keeps its leaves through the year
senses.definitionCN: 形容植物一年四季开花或常绿
senses.example: A border of perpetual flowers lined the garden path.
senses.exampleCN: 一圈四季开花的植物沿着花园小径两列排开。
senses.why: Gardeners borrow the lasting idea for plants that keep flowering instead of fading once.
senses.whyCN: 园艺者借用「持久」这层意思，形容不只在一次花期开放、而是一直在开的植物。

intro.en: Perpetual comes from Latin perpetuus, continuous or uninterrupted, a word of debated formation beside the verb perpeti.
intro.cn: perpetual 来自拉丁语 perpetuus（连续的、不间断的），关于其构词有多种解释，一般认为与动词 perpeti（承受到底、持续）有关。

items.en: Perpetuus means continuous, unbroken, and whole.
items.cn: perpetuus 意为连续的、不间断的、完整的。

items.en: The older verb perpeti, to bear through, is often cited as its companion.
items.cn: 更早的动词 perpeti（一路承受下去）常被视为与它相伴的来源。

items.en: Christian writers extend the word to meanings of eternal life.
items.cn: 基督教作家把这个词扩展到「永生」等宗教含义。

items.en: From French, the adjective enters English alongside related nouns.
items.cn: 经由法语，这个形容词连同相关名词一起进入英语。

items.en: Middle English adopts perpetual with its lasting sense intact.
items.cn: 中古英语吸收 perpetual，保留了「持久」的核心含义。

items.en: Modern English also uses it in set phrases such as perpetual snow and perpetual motion.
items.cn: 现代英语还在 perpetual snow、perpetual motion 等固定说法里使用它。

note.en: Perpetual should not be confused with perpetrate, which sounds close but describes committing a crime, and it sits beside permanent and endless.
note.cn: perpetual 易与读音相近的 perpetrate 混淆，后者意为「犯下罪行」，两者词源不同；含义上它靠近 permanent 与 endless。

entries.definition: to commit a crime or a wrong act
entries.definitionCN: 犯罪；干坏事（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: always, or again and again
to make something last or continue
lasting or meant to last for a long time
having no end or limit
lasting for ever, or seeming to

normalIntro.en: Perpetual borrows the prefix per-, meaning through, and it describes things that keep running all the way.
normalIntro.cn: perpetual 借用前缀 per-（贯穿），形容一路运行下去、没有尽头的事物。

normal.en: Perpetual and perpetrate share the per- prefix, so keep the lasting and the criminal apart.
normal.cn: perpetual 与 perpetrate 都带 per- 前缀，要分清「持久」与「犯罪」两回事。

normal.en: The adverb perpetually means again and again.
normal.cn: 副词 perpetually 表示一次又一次、不停地。

normal.en: Perpetual snow is the snow on high peaks that never melts.
normal.cn: perpetual snow 指高山之上终年不化的积雪。

normal.en: The verb perpetuate switches families: it means to keep something going.
normal.cn: 动词 perpetuate 换了词性：意指让某事延续下去。

normal.en: Compare permanent: permanent is by plan, perpetual is by fate.
normal.cn: 对比 permanent：permanent 多是出于安排，perpetual 更像一直如此、无从终结。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum swinging on and on through the night.
abstract.cn: 想象钟摆整夜摇过来又摇过去。

abstract.en: Picture a foghorn sounding again and again over the harbour.
abstract.cn: 想象雾笛在海港上空一遍又一遍地鸣响。

abstract.en: Picture a ring around your finger that never ends.
abstract.cn: 想象指上的一枚戒指，绕成一圈，没有终点。

examples.en: They live in fear of perpetual war.
examples.cn: 他们活在无休止战争的恐惧里。

examples.en: The motor kept up a perpetual roar.
examples.cn: 马达一直发出轰鸣。

examples.en: She smiled with perpetual good humour.
examples.cn: 她总是带着好心情微笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼拍锤偶」——水泼上去、拍打、锤子敲个不停，怎么也停不下来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 perpetuus（连续的、不间断的）→ 经法语进入英语 perpetual；一般认为与 perpeti（一路承受、持续下去）相关，前缀 per- 表「贯穿到底」。

sensesIntro.en: Perpetual starts from lasting for ever, leans into the sense of never stopping, and is borrowed by gardeners for plants that flower all year.
sensesIntro.cn: perpetual 从「永远持续」出发，偏向「不停歇」的含义，又被园艺借来形容四季开花的植物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pendulum that circles on without a stop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈接一圈、永不停下的钟摆。

branches.en: Enduring without end is the base sense.
branches.cn: 没有尽头地持续是基础义项。

branches.en: Something never ending also never truly stops.
branches.cn: 永不结束的东西也就从不真正停下。

branches.en: Gardeners extend the lasting idea to plants.
branches.cn: 园艺者把「持久」义延伸到植物。

branches.en: An endless fear and an eternal love share one image of continuity.
branches.cn: 无尽的恐惧与永恒的爱共享同一个「连续不断」的意象。

branches.en: Things that never stop, whether hums or flowers, fit the middle ground.
branches.cn: 从嗡嗡声到一年四季的花，凡是停不下来的事物都落在中间地带。

intro.en: Perpetual pairs the Latin prefix per- with a root seen in the verb perpeti, and adds the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: perpetual 由拉丁语前缀 per-、见于动词 perpeti 的词根与形容词词尾 -al 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin per- means through, and the ending -al marks an adjective of quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 per- 表示「贯穿」，词尾 -al 标记性质形容词。

items.example: The prefix per- suggests running through time.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 per- 暗示贯穿时间。

items.example: Perpetuus is the direct ancestor of perpetual.
items.exampleCN: perpetuus 是 perpetual 的直接祖先。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -al shapes the adjective perpetual.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 塑造了形容词 perpetual。

items.example: Perpeti is often cited beside perpetuus.
items.exampleCN: perpeti 常被视为与 perpetuus 相伴。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms perpetually.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 perpetually。

items.example: Perpetually describes how something keeps going.
items.exampleCN: perpetually 描述某事持续不断。

items.example: Perpetuate turns the lasting sense into an action.
items.exampleCN: perpetuate 把持久的含义变成动作。

items.example: Perpetuate keeps a custom alive.
items.exampleCN: perpetuate 让习俗延续下去。

items.meaning: the state of lasting for ever
items.example: Perpetuity is the abstract noun of lasting time.
items.exampleCN: perpetuity 是表示持久时间的抽象名词。

items.meaning: a person who commits a crime
items.example: Perpetrator belongs to perpetrare, a different root.
items.exampleCN: perpetrator 属于另一个词根 perpetrare。

definition_zh: 使永久化；使延续不断；使（错误、偏见、做法等）长期存在；使保持原状（多见于正式用语）
definition_en: to make something such as a belief, practice, or problem continue for a long time, often longer than it should
core_image: 一只脚踩在别人的脚印上，把同一条路越踩越深
scene: 祖辈相传的渔歌每年开渔都要唱一遍，年轻人跟着老人学，从没断过。The village continues to perpetuate its fishing songs by teaching them to the youngest children.
sceneCN: 这里 perpetuate 是「使延续、使代代相传」（第 2 个义项：让习俗与做法一直传下去）；句意为村里把渔歌教给最小的孩子，让这门代代传唱的习俗不断延续。画面里是被踩得很深的同一条小路，喻指重复本身让事物留了下来。

pos.zh: 使永久化；使延续；使长期存在
使（谬误、偏见、不公做法等）延续下去；纵容其留存

collocations.zh: 延续一个错误传说；让某个误解流传

derivatives.zh: perpetu 加 -al 构成，义为「永久的；持续不断的」
perpetual 加 -ly 构成，义为「永远地；持续不断地」
perpetuate 加 -ion 构成，义为「延续；永久化」
perpetu 加 -ity 构成，义为「永久；永续（多用于法律：in perpetuity 永久地）」
perpetuate 加 -or 构成，义为「使某事延续的人；助长者」

senses.title: Keep something going without end
senses.definition: to cause something to exist or continue without a natural end
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物存在或持续下去，没有自然的终点
senses.example: The foundation was created to perpetuate the memory of its founder.
senses.exampleCN: 这个基金会的设立是为了让创办人的精神永久留存。
senses.why: The Latin verb perpetuare is built on perpetuus, which means lasting through, unbroken; to perpetuate is to push a thing towards that unbroken state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 perpetuare 建立在 perpetuus 之上，后者意为「贯穿始终、不中断」；perpetuate 就是把事物推向这种不中断的状态。

senses.title: Hand a practice on to the next generation
senses.definition: to make a custom, skill, or habit pass from one generation to the next
senses.definitionCN: 使习俗、技艺或习惯从一代人传到下一代人
senses.example: Elders perpetuate the old songs by singing them at every harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 长者们每逢收获都唱这些老歌，让它们代代相传。
senses.why: The root per- adds the idea of through, so the continuous state is imagined as a thread running through time rather than as a single act.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 per- 带来「贯穿」的意思，因此这种持续被想象成穿行于时间中的一根线，而不是一次性的动作。

senses.title: Keep a mistake or prejudice alive
senses.titleCN: 让错误与偏见长期存活
senses.definition: to keep an error, myth, or prejudice in circulation instead of correcting it
senses.definitionCN: 让错误、误解或偏见继续流传，而不去纠正它
senses.example: Repeating the myth perpetuates a false picture of the past.
senses.exampleCN: 反复讲述那个传说，等于让一幅虚假的往昔图景一直流传。
senses.why: A false belief survives because people keep passing it on; to perpetuate is to keep handing it down, and the word becomes almost an accusation when the object is a myth.
senses.whyCN: 错误的信念因为人们不断转述而存活；perpetuate 就是不断把它递出去，当对象是谬误时，这个词几乎成了指责。

senses.title: Enlarge an advantage already held
senses.titleCN: 把已有的差距越拉越大
senses.definition: to make an existing position or gap continue and grow, especially a gap between groups
senses.definitionCN: 使既有的状况或差距继续存在并扩大，尤指群体之间的差距
senses.example: Unequal funding perpetuates the gap between rich and poor schools.
senses.exampleCN: 不平等的拨款让富裕学校与贫困学校之间的差距长期存在。
senses.why: What continues also keeps producing its own effects; in sociology the word often names a loop in which an advantage reproduces itself.
senses.whyCN: 继续存在的东西也在继续产生自己的后果；在社会学的用法里，这个词常指优势自我复制的循环。

senses.title: Keep a state unchanged on purpose
senses.definition: to keep a situation as it is on purpose, often to protect it
senses.definitionCN: 有意让某种状况保持原样，常带保护之意
senses.example: The treaty was designed to perpetuate the balance between the two powers.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约的用意是让两个强权之间的平衡一直维持下去。
senses.why: Adjective and verb here carry no judgement: preserving what works is the same act as freezing what does not, and the context decides.
senses.whyCN: 形容词与动词本身并不作评判：保留有用的东西与冻结无用的东西是同一个动作，由语境决定褒贬。

senses.title: Let an office or right last with no limit
senses.definition: in law and official writing, to make a right, office, or arrangement last indefinitely
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与正式文字中，使某项权利、职位或安排无限期地延续
senses.example: The charter perpetuates the council as the final arbiter.
senses.exampleCN: 这份章程让该委员会永久担任最终裁决者。
senses.why: English legal use keeps the oldest latin colour: perpetual tenure and perpetual rent were phrases of property law before perpetuate became a general verb.
senses.whyCN: 英语的法律用法保留了最古老的拉丁色调：perpetual tenure 与 perpetual rent 这类说法在 perpetuate 成为一般动词之前，已是财产法里的用语。

senses.title: Make something survive longer than expected
senses.definition: to make a thing or person live on far longer than anyone expected
senses.definitionCN: 使某物或某人在远超过预期的年头里仍然存续
senses.example: The memoir perpetuated his name long after the scandal faded.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻早已淡去，那本回忆录却让他的名字久久留存。
senses.why: Survival past the expected end is the everyday image of lasting; the verb simply switches the question from what lasts to who or what makes it last.
senses.whyCN: 熬过预期的终点是「持久」最日常的画面；动词只是把问题从「什么在持续」换成了「谁让它持续」。

senses.title: Keep a wrong going by not stopping it
senses.definition: to allow a harmful thing to continue by repeating it or failing to stop it
senses.definitionCN: 通过重复或不加阻止，让有害之事继续下去
senses.example: Silence on the playground perpetuates the bullying.
senses.exampleCN: 校园里的沉默让霸凌一直延续。
senses.why: Not acting can perpetuate as surely as acting; the verb then names complicity rather than intention, which is why it so often appears in policy writing.
senses.whyCN: 不作为和作为一样能让事物延续；此时动词命名的是共谋而非意图，这正是它频繁出现在政策文字中的原因。

intro.en: Perpetuate comes from Latin perpetuare, made from perpetuus, "continuous, lasting all the way through", which is itself built on petere, "to go towards". The core is not a long time but an unbroken course.
intro.cn: perpetuate 来自拉丁语 perpetuare，出自 perpetuus「连续的、贯穿到底的」，而这个词又建立在 petere「向……去」之上。核心不是很长的时间，而是一段不间断的路程。

items.en: The reconstructed root *pet- gives Latin petere, "to seek, to go towards", and English feather and compete also trace back to related forms.
items.cn: 重构词根 *pet- 衍生出拉丁语 petere「追求、向……去」，英语 feather 与 compete 也来自相关形式。

items.en: Petere means to go towards, to seek, and in legal use to sue or claim. It supplies the motion at the heart of perpetuate.
items.cn: petere 意为「向……去、追求」，在法律用语中还有「诉求、起诉」之义；perpetuate 核心的动感就来自它。

items.en: Per- "through" plus the pet- stem gives perpetuus, "continuous, running through without a break", and the adverb perpetuo, "constantly".
items.cn: 前缀 per-「贯穿」加 pet- 词干构成 perpetuus，意为「连续的、一路不间断的」，另有副词 perpetuo「不断地」。

items.en: Perpetuare means to make lasting or eternal, used of keeping a state in being. The English verb is borrowed from this form.
items.cn: perpetuare 意为「使持久、使永存」，用来表示让某种状态一直存在；英语动词直接借自这一形式。

items.en: English perpetuate is recorded in the sixteenth century, first with the neutral sense of keeping something in being, then by the nineteenth century also as criticism of keeping errors alive.
items.cn: 英语 perpetuate 见于十六世纪，先是中性的「使存续」，到十九世纪又常带批评色彩，指让谬误继续存活。

items.en: Modern usage adds fixed phrases such as perpetuate stereotypes, perpetuate inequality and perpetuate the cycle, where the object is a problem rather than a treasure.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了 perpetuate stereotypes、perpetuate inequality、perpetuate the cycle 等固定说法，这些说法里的对象是问题而不是珍宝。

note.en: The look-alike group contains the adjective and nouns built on the same latin stem; the near-meaning group separates other verbs of keeping something in being.
note.cn: 形近组收同词干构成的形容词与名词；近义组区分其他表示「使某物继续存在」的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective of endless duration, nearest cousin of perpetuate and the word most often confused with it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「永久的；不断的」。是同根词里与 perpetuate 最接近、最容易被混淆的一个，记「形容词 perpetua、动词 perpetua 加 te」。

entries.definition: The adverb of the same family, meaning without stopping.
entries.definitionCN: 同族副词，义为「永久地；不断地」。

entries.definition: The noun of the action, the act of keeping something going.
entries.definitionCN: 动作名词，义为「延续；永久化」。

entries.definition: The state of lasting forever, common in phrases such as in perpetuity.
entries.definitionCN: 永久的状态，常见于 in perpetuity「永久地」这类短语。

entries.definition: To make something last longer than planned. It measures time only and carries no judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物比原计划更久地延续，只计时间，不含褒贬。

entries.definition: To keep something in good condition, usually with approval, where perpetuate may be either approval or blame.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物保持良好状态，通常带肯定意味；perpetuate 则可能褒可能贬。

entries.definition: To keep something going with effort or support, as effort is put into sustaining a habit.
entries.definitionCN: 靠努力或支持使某物持续，强调持续需要投入。

entries.definition: To spread an idea or practice widely, which is what keeps it alive; perpetuate stresses duration rather than reach.
entries.definitionCN: 传播观念或做法，传播本身使其存活；perpetuate 更强调时长而不是范围。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin per- "through" plus petere "go towards", giving perpetuus, perpetuare, and the English family perpetual, perpetually, perpetuation, perpetuity.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 per-「贯穿」加 petere「向……去」，构成 perpetuus、perpetuare，英语词族有 perpetual、perpetually、perpetuation、perpetuity。

normal.en: Per- means through and petere means go towards, so perpetuate is about a course that runs through time.
normal.cn: per- 意为「贯穿」，petere 意为「向……去」，所以 perpetuate 说的是贯穿时间的路程。

normal.en: Family check: adjective perpetual, adverb perpetually, action noun perpetuation, legal noun perpetuity.
normal.cn: 同族核对：形容词 perpetual，副词 perpetually，动作名词 perpetuation，法律名词 perpetuity。

normal.en: The usual objects are bad things: perpetuate a myth, perpetuate inequality, perpetuate the cycle.
normal.cn: 常见对象多是坏东西：延续误解、让不平等长存、让循环转下去。

normal.en: If a person or a school perpetuates something, the real subject is repetition carried out by people.
normal.cn: 如果某人或某校 perpetuate 某物，真正起作用的是人们在完成的重复。

normal.en: Do not mix the adjective perpetual with the verb perpetuate: one describes, the other makes a thing last.
normal.cn: 别把形容词 perpetual 与动词 perpetuate 混用：一个是在描述，一个是在让事物延续。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of feet stepping into the same prints again and again, until the path is worn deep.
abstract.cn: 想象一双脚一次次踩进同样的脚印，把那条路踩得越来越深。

abstract.en: Picture a thread being passed from hand to hand down a long line of people.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线在长长的人群里，从一只手递到另一只手。

abstract.en: Picture a building held up by the same beams, kept standing only by constant repair.
abstract.cn: 想象一座仅靠不断修补才立着的房子，靠的是同一批梁柱。

examples.en: Some textbooks perpetuate the myth that Rome fell in a single night.
examples.cn: 有些教科书让「罗马一夜之间崩塌」这个传说一直流传。

examples.en: School uniforms may perpetuate outdated ideas about how girls should dress.
examples.cn: 校服可能让关于女孩应如何穿着的旧观念长期存在。

examples.en: By refusing to intervene, the principal perpetuated an unfair rule for another year.
examples.cn: 校长拒绝介入，使一条不公平的规定又多存在了一年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼泼丢特」——把一件事泼出去、丢不掉，于是它就一直重复下去；这仅是谐音，与词源无关。

root: 源自拉丁语 perpetuare，出自 perpetuus「连续的、贯穿始终的」，由前缀 per-「贯穿、彻底」加 petere「向……去」构成；核心是「一路走下去、不中断」。

sensesIntro.en: One image holds eight senses: whatever is repeated keeps standing, whether it is a treasured song, a false myth, a widening gap, a protected balance, an endless office, a name that outlives a scandal, or a silence that lets a wrong continue.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个意象撑起八个义项：被重复的东西就一直还在。它可以是珍爱的歌谣、错误的传说、越拉越大的差距、被保护的平衡、没有期限的职位、熬过丑闻的名字，也可以是不加阻止的沉默。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footsteps pressed into the same path until the ground is worn down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双脚一次次踩在同一条路上，把地面踩实、踩深。

branches.en: ENDLESS EXISTENCE: a thing is made to have no natural end.
branches.cn: 无终之存：使事物没有自然的终点。

branches.en: TIME: a custom travels to the next generation and an office runs without a term.
branches.cn: 时间：习俗传给下一代，职位没有任期。

branches.en: KEEPING WHAT SHOULD GO: a myth or a wrong is kept alive by repetition or by silence.
branches.cn: 留住该走的：谬误靠重复存活，错误靠沉默延续。

branches.en: LOOP: an advantage keeps reproducing itself and widens the gap.
branches.cn: 循环：优势不断自我复制，差距越拉越大。

branches.en: NO JUDGEMENT: protecting a balance or letting a name outlive a scandal says nothing about good or bad.
branches.cn: 不作评判：保护平衡，或让名字熬过丑闻，都不说明好坏。

intro.en: Perpetuate is a verb carved from a latin adjective, and its endings mark the person, the state, and the endlessness of a right.
intro.cn: perpetuate 是从拉丁形容词削出来的动词，它的词尾分别标记行为人、状态与权利的无限期。

latinIntro.en: The working pieces are per- "through", petere "go towards", perpet- (the stem), -u- (adjective vowel), and -are, the latin verb ending; English adds -ate, -ous, -al, -ion, -ity, -or.
latinIntro.cn: 可用的构件是 per-「贯穿」、petere「向……去」、词干 perpet-、连接元音 -u- 以及拉丁动词词尾 -are；英语再加 -ate、-ous、-al、-ion、-ity、-or。

items.example: The prefix fixes the length: through.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀规定了长度：贯穿到底。

items.example: Petere supplies the motion of the word.
items.exampleCN: petere 提供这个词的动感。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of an unbroken course.
items.exampleCN: 词干承载「不间断的路程」这一想法。

items.meaning: to make, to cause to be
items.example: The ending turns a state into an act.
items.exampleCN: 词尾把状态变成动作。

items.example: The suffix forms the adjective of state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成状态形容词。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: The suffix makes the state abstract.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把状态抽象化。

items.example: The suffix marks the manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记方式。

items.example: Old latin adjectives used this ending, which shows in the stem.
items.exampleCN: 古拉丁形容词用这个词尾，这在词干上看得出来。

items.meaningCN: 永久；永续（常见于 in perpetuity）
items.example: The land was granted in perpetuity.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地被永久授予。

derivatives.zh: 永久的；不断的
永远地；不断地
延续；永久化
永久；永续

definition_zh: 使困惑；使迷惑不解；使迷惑为难；使复杂化；（被动）感到为难
definition_en: to make someone feel confused and unable to think clearly, usually because a problem or question is complicated
core_image: 一副没织完的线团在桌上缠成一团，越理越乱
scene: 学生在图书馆看那份试卷，题干里连着两层否定，读到第三遍还是理不清要在问什么。The double negative in the question perplexed even the best students.
sceneCN: 这里 perplexed 是「使困惑、让人摸不着头脑」（第 1 个义项：被复杂的问题弄得想不清楚）；句意为题干里的双重否定连最好的学生也搞糊涂了。画面里缠乱的线团，正是问题在心里越缠越紧的样子。

pos.zh: 使复杂化；使纠缠不清（古旧用法）
（多见于旧译，今常用 perplexed）困惑的；为难的

derivatives.zh: perplex 加 -ed 构成，义为「困惑的；不知所措的」
perplex 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人困惑的」
perplex 换成 -ity 词尾，义为「困惑；难题」
perplexing 加 -ly 构成，义为「令人困惑地」

senses.title: Throw the mind into confusion
senses.definition: to make someone unable to think clearly because something is too complicated or unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 因某事过于复杂或出乎意料，使某人无法清楚地思考
senses.example: The rule has three exceptions, each with a further exception.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则有三个例外，而每个例外之下又有例外，听完让人愈发困惑。
senses.why: Latin perplexus is per- "thoroughly" plus plectere "to weave"; a thoroughly woven thing is a knot the eye cannot follow, and that is what the mind becomes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 perplexus 是 per-「彻底」加 plectere「编织」：被彻底编织起来的东西，眼睛跟不住线，于是脑子也跟不住。

senses.title: Pose an unusually hard question
senses.definition: of a question, riddle, or problem, to be so difficult that it blocks anyone who meets it
senses.definitionCN: 指某个问题、谜语或难题异常难解，把遇到它的人挡住
senses.example: The riddle perplexed every traveller who tried to answer it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个谜语难倒了每一个想回答它的旅人。
senses.why: A question can perplex by itself, without a person to blame. The subject moves from the mind to the problem, since the weave belongs to the problem.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题本身就能让人困惑，不必有人负责。主语从「头脑」转到「问题」上，因为乱的是问题那一团线。

senses.title: Puzzle in an admiring or playful way
senses.titleCN: 带着好奇与赞叹地费解
senses.definition: of a fact or sight, to fill the mind with wonder mixed with confusion
senses.definitionCN: 指某种事实或景象让人既费解又惊奇
senses.example: The geometry of the hive has perplexed biologists for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 蜂巢的几何结构让生物学家费解了好几百年。
senses.why: When the mystery is a pleasure rather than a nuisance, perplex takes the warmer colour of wonder, and it survives in this wider tone.
senses.whyCN: 当谜团是一种乐趣而不是麻烦，perplex 便带上惊奇这种更温暖的色调，并在这一层意义上延续下来。

senses.title: Complicate and entangle a matter
senses.definition: in older use, to entangle a matter or make it more complicated than it needs to be
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的用法中，指把事情纠缠起来，或使其比本来应有的更加复杂
senses.example: The new clause only perplexed an argument that was nearly settled.
senses.exampleCN: 新条款把一个本已接近谈拢的争论又搅乱了。
senses.why: The literal image of weaving is closest here: the word once meant tangling things, not only tangling minds.
senses.whyCN: 这里最接近「编织」的字面意象：这个词当初既指把东西缠乱，也指把脑子缠乱。

senses.title: To sit there as the confused one
senses.definition: as an adjective, to be in a state of confusion or hesitation about what to do
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词时，指对下一步该做什么感到困惑或迟疑
senses.example: She stood perplexed at the crossing with no signpost.
senses.exampleCN: 她站在没有路标的路口，不知道往哪走。
senses.why: The participle form asks about the person, not the cause. Modern English prefers perplexed, while perplex as an adjective survives in older and literary text.
senses.whyCN: 分词形式关心的是人而不是原因。现代英语更常用 perplexed，余下的 perplex 作形容词多见于较早或文学性的文字。

senses.title: Make the reader work hard
senses.definition: of a text or account, to be obscure or puzzling enough to slow the reader down
senses.definitionCN: 指文字或叙述晦涩难懂，让读者不得不放慢速度
senses.example: His lecture notes perplexed more students than the exam did.
senses.exampleCN: 他的讲义比考试本身更让学生糊涂。
senses.why: Woven prose is one more kind of knot. The same verb moves from the subject of writing to the object of reading.
senses.whyCN: 织得过分密的文字也是另一种线团：同一个动词从写作的一方，走到了阅读的一方。

intro.en: Perplex comes from Latin perplexus, "interwoven, entangled", from plectere, "to weave". The confusion it names is physical before it is mental, a knot the eye cannot follow.
intro.cn: perplex 来自拉丁语 perplexus「交织的、缠结的」，出自 plectere「编织」。它命名的困惑先是身体的、后才是心里的：一个眼睛跟不住线的结。

items.en: A reconstructed root *plek- "to plait, weave, fold" underlies Latin plectere and English plait, pleat, and ply word forms, all built on the idea of something folded or twisted together.
items.cn: 重构词根 *plek-「编、织、折」是拉丁语 plectere 与英语 plait、pleat、ply 等词的底层，都建立在「交织、折叠」这一观念上。

items.en: Plectere means to plait, weave, or twist, and it also appears in complexus (intertwined) and in nexus (a tying).
items.cn: plectere 意为「编、织、缠绕」，也见于 complexus（交织的）与 nexus（系结）。

items.en: Per- "thoroughly" plus plectere gives perplexus, "thoroughly woven, entangled", used of paths and arguments.
items.cn: 前缀 per-「彻底」加 plectere 构成 perplexus，意为「彻底编织在一起的、缠结的」，用于道路与论证。

items.en: English perplex, first as an adjective in the fifteenth century and then as a verb, kept the twist: to entangle, and so to confuse.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪先出现形容词 perplex，后出现动词，一直保留「缠绕」的动作：缠在一起，因此迷惑。

items.en: The adjective was largely replaced by perplexed, while the verb settled on the confusion of the mind; perplexity keeps both the state and the puzzle.
items.cn: 形容词大多被 perplexed 取代，动词固定指头脑的困惑；perplexity 则兼指状态与难题。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the weave: words sharing the plaiting root; the near-meaning group ranks other words for confusion from mild to severe.
note.cn: 形近组沿着「编织」展开，收共享这一词根的词；近义组按困惑程度由轻到重排列。

entries.definition: The usual adjective of the person, meaning confused about what to think or do.
entries.definitionCN: 常用形容词，形容人「困惑的；不知所措的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being confused, and also for a hard puzzle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「困惑」，也指难解的难题。

entries.definition: From com- "together" and plectere: woven together, hence complicated. A different prefix on the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「一起」与 plectere 构成：编织在一起，因此复杂。与 perplex 不同前缀的同根词。

entries.definition: The adjective of the thing that puzzles, used for questions, situations, and results.
entries.definitionCN: 形容令人困惑的东西，用于问题、情境与结果。

entries.definition: The plain everyday word for muddling the mind; perplex is rarer and suggests a knot rather than a brief muddle.
entries.definitionCN: 最日常的「使糊涂」，perplex 较少见，且暗示一个结而不是一时的糊涂。

entries.definition: To confuse completely by too many options; it conveys a stronger sense of being lost than perplex does.
entries.definitionCN: 因选择太多而彻底迷惑；比 perplex 更强调「迷路」的感觉。

entries.definition: To puzzle in a way that also suggests secrecy, often of a person or an organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 令人费解，常暗示某种隐情，多用于人或机构。

entries.definition: To defeat understanding entirely, used of things that defeat explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 使完全无法理解，用于无法解释的事物。

entries.definition: To make someone nervous and confused, so that they hurry and making mistakes.
entries.definitionCN: 使人心慌意乱，以致匆忙出错。

normalIntro.en: Real parts: Latin per- "through" plus plectere "to weave", and a family of perplexed, perplexing, perplexity set beside complex and nexus, which share the same plaiting root.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 per-「彻底」加 plectere「编织」，词族有 perplexed、perplexing、perplexity，并且与 complex、nexus 共享「编织」这条词根。

normal.en: Plectere meant to weave, so perplex is to have your thoughts woven into a knot.
normal.cn: plectere 意为「编织」，所以 perplex 就是思绪被编成了一个结。

normal.en: Compare complex: both come from plectere, but com- joins and per- goes through, so one is joined, the other tangled.
normal.cn: 对比 complex：二者都出自 plectere，但 com- 表「合在一起」，per- 表「贯穿」，一个是被拼合，一个是被缠死。

normal.en: The person is perplexed, and the problem is perplexing; the pair keeps -ed for the one and -ing for the other.
normal.cn: 人是 perplexed，问题是 perplexing；带 -ed 的形容人，带 -ing 的形容事。

normal.en: Perplexity is both the feeling and the puzzle, as clear as the verb is, the noun is broader.
normal.cn: perplexity 既是那种感受，也是那桩难题：名词比动词涵盖得更宽。

normal.en: Old plait, pleat, and ply belong to the same weaving family as the verb.
normal.cn: 较早的 plait、pleat、ply 与这个动词同属「编织」这个词族。

abstract.en: Picture a ball of wool on a table, and every pull of the hand makes the knot tighter.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上一个毛线球，每拉一下，结就勒得更紧。

abstract.en: Picture a maze with walls that move each time you turn a corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一座迷宫，每转过一个拐角，墙就自己挪一次位。

abstract.en: Picture a rope twisted from three strands, and the pattern is beautiful until you try to name which strand is which.
abstract.cn: 想象一根由三股拧成的绳子，图案很美，直到你想说清哪一股是哪一股。

examples.en: The mechanics of the clock perplexed the apprentice for weeks.
examples.cn: 这座钟的机械原理让学徒困惑了好几周。

examples.en: Her calm answer to so hostile a question left the panel perplexed.
examples.cn: 面对如此敌意的问题，她平静的回答让评审团摸不着头脑。

examples.en: Nothing about the tide perplexes the old fishermen.
examples.cn: 这些潮水的规律对老渔民来说没有一点费解之处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破不来克斯」——线索破了、怎么都来不了，脑子缠成一团；这仅是谐音，与词源无关。

root: 源自拉丁语 perplexus「彻底编织在一起的」，由 per-「彻底」加 plectere「编织」构成；同一词根还见于 complex「复杂的」与 nexus「联系」；核心是「缠成一团」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all follow the weave: a mind is tangled, a question blocks whoever meets it, the tangle may arrive as wonder, a matter may be knotted and complicated, a person may be the knot, and writing can knot a reader.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都沿着「编织」展开：思绪被缠成一团，问题是挡在面前的结，这团结也可能以惊奇的面貌到来，事情可以被搅乱、变得更复杂，人可以成为那个结，文字也能把读者缠住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tangled ball of thread that tightens with every attempt to unwind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：缠成一团的线，每想解开一次，就收得更紧。

branches.en: MIND: the first and central sense, a tangled and slow mind.
branches.cn: 心思：最核心的义项，被缠住、转不动的头脑。

branches.en: TEXT: questions and writing can knot whoever meets them.
branches.cn: 文本：问题与文字能把遇到它的人缠住。

branches.en: WONDER: the same tangle, viewed as attractive rather than annoying.
branches.cn: 惊奇：同一团结，被看成吸引人而不是扰人的。

branches.en: MATTER: the literal strand, a matter knotted into needless complexity.
branches.cn: 事情：最字面的一股线，把事情缠成不必要的复杂。

branches.en: PERSON: the participle puts a human at the centre of the knot.

intro.en: Perplex is a verb made from a latin participle, and English adds the endings that place the confusion in a person, in a thing, or in a name.
intro.cn: perplex 是从拉丁分词做成的动词，英语再加词尾，把困惑分别安在人身上、事物身上或名词上。

latinIntro.en: The reliable pieces are per- "through", plectere "to weave", and the participle perplexus, whose stem gives the English verb; plexus is the weave itself.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠构件是 per-「彻底」、plectere「编织」与分词 perplexus，词干形成英语动词；plexus 就是那团编织本身。

senses.title: Something extra that comes with the post
senses.titleCN: 随职位附带的额外供给
senses.definition: an extra payment or benefit supplied with a job, over and above the normal wage
senses.definitionCN: 在工资之外，随职务额外提供的一笔报酬或福利
senses.example: The post came with the perquisite of a hospital car.
senses.exampleCN: 这个职位附带一项待遇：可以使用医院的公车。
senses.why: Latin perquirere means to seek thoroughly; a perquisite is the thing sought out and claimed on top of what is owned, a right hunted down beyond the salary.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 perquirere 意为「彻底寻求」；perquisite 就是除本分收入之外，被一再追寻并主张到手的东西。

senses.title: A special privilege of rank
senses.definition: a special right attached to a rank or position rather than to work done
senses.definitionCN: 指附着于级别或职位、而非附着于所完成工作的特殊权利
senses.example: The perquisite of a private seat in the gallery is still defended.
senses.exampleCN: 在楼座拥有一席私座的这项特权至今仍被维护。
senses.why: A privilege is not paid for; it is attached. The older sense of a right claimed alongside a holding explains this legal flavour.
senses.whyCN: 特权不是被支付出来的，而是被附着上去的。较早那层「随占有物一并主张的权利」之意，解释了这种法律气味。

senses.title: A legal right attached to property
senses.titleCN: 随财产附带的权利（法律）
senses.definition: in law, a profit or right enjoyed along with a property by a person who does not own it
senses.definitionCN: 法律中指非所有人随某项财产一并享有的一种收益或权利
senses.example: Collecting the fruit from the orchard was an old perquisite of the tenant.
senses.exampleCN: 采摘果园里的果实曾是承租人一项古老的附带权利。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded layer: a right that rides along with a property. Jobs later became the property and wages the owner, so the word moved to pay and privilege.
senses.whyCN: 这是记录中最早的一层：随财产一并运行的权利。后来职位成了那份财产，工资成了物主，于是这个词转向了薪金与特权。

senses.title: A casual extra income
senses.definition: in older use, an incidental source of money beyond the stated fee
senses.definitionCN: 较早用法中指超出约定费用之外的偶然进项
senses.example: The clerk counted his perquisites from copying letters on the side.
senses.exampleCN: 那位文书把私下替人抄信的零碎进项盘算了一遍。
senses.why: Before salaries were fixed, income came in casual pieces; a perquisite was one of those pieces, extra and incidental.
senses.whyCN: 在薪资制度固定之前，收入是一份份零散得来的；perquisite 就是其中额外、偶然的一份。

senses.title: Any extra reward of a job
senses.titleCN: 工作带来的任何额外收获
senses.definition: the general modern sense: anything extra a job brings beyond the pay
senses.definitionCN: 现代一般义：工作除工资之外带来的任何额外好处
senses.example: Travel and the chance to learn a language are perquisites of this work.
senses.exampleCN: 出差的机会和学一门语言的机会，都是这份工作的额外收获。
senses.why: The word generalised from legal rights to workplace perks, and the short form perk now does most of the everyday work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法律权利泛化到工作福利，日常的主要任务如今由口语缩写 perk 承担。

senses.title: A benefit of office that looks illegitimate
senses.titleCN: 看着像特权的公家好处
senses.definition: a benefit of office that critics see as an unfair privilege
senses.definitionCN: 批评者视为不当特权的公职好处
senses.example: Ministers were challenged over the perquisites of their office.
senses.exampleCN: 部长们因职务待遇问题受到质询。
senses.why: Because a perquisite is attached rather than earned, critics can question it: this use is close to the Latin sense of something sought for oneself.
senses.whyCN: 因为待遇是附着而来而非挣来的，批评者便能质疑它：这一用法贴近拉丁语里「为自己求得的东西」之意。

intro.en: Perquisite comes from Latin perquiritur, "it is sought for", built on perquirere, "to search thoroughly outside ones own property". The word names a thing hunted out and claimed, which is why its oldest sense is a legal right of a tenant.
intro.cn: perquisite 来自拉丁语 perquiritur「它被彻底求得」，建立在 perquirere「彻底搜寻」之上。这个词命名的是被寻得并主张到手的东西，所以最早的一层是承租人的附带权利。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, search for, ask for, and it also gives quaestio and the English words question and quest.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求、寻找、探问」，也衍生出拉丁语 quaestio 与英语的 question 和 quest。

items.en: Per- "thoroughly" plus quaerere gives perquirere, to search thoroughly, and in legal use to seek a right or profit attached to another persons property.
items.cn: 前缀 per-「彻底」加 quaerere 构成 perquirere，意为「彻底搜寻」，在法律用法中指为依附于他人财产的权利或收益而寻求。

items.en: The past participle perquisitum, a thing thoroughly sought, entered law as a right claimed alongside a holding, the oldest layer of this word.
items.cn: 过去分词 perquisitum 意为「彻底求得之物」，进入法律后指随某项占有物一并主张的权利，这是这个词最早的一层。

items.en: English perquisite appears in the fifteenth century with rights and casual profits attached to an office, including the right to keep certain fees or profits.
items.cn: 英语 perquisite 见于十五世纪，指附着于职位的权利与零星收益，包括有权留下某些费用或利润。

items.en: As salaries became the main form of pay, perquisite spread to the goods and other benefits given with a post; the clipped form perk appears in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 当薪金成为主要报酬形式，perquisite 扩展到随职位提供的物品与其他福利；截短形式 perk 出现在十九世纪。

items.en: Source uncertain on one point: some dictionaries link the spelling to a Latin perquisitum, but its exact legal wording differs from source to source.
items.cn: 有一处存疑：部分词典把拼写追溯到拉丁语 perquisitum，但各处记载的法律措辞并不完全一致。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the short form perk and the latin seek-words that share the quaerere root; the near-meaning group separates other words for extra pay.
note.cn: 形近组收截短形式 perk 与共享 quaerere「寻求」词根的词；近义组按性质区分其他表示额外收入的词。

entries.definition: The everyday short form of perquisite, used for pay, travel, and office benefits.
entries.definitionCN: perquisite 的日常短形式，用于薪资、差旅、办公福利等。

entries.definition: Something required rather than extra. It only looks like perquisite; the prefix differs and the meaning is close to opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 指「必需品」而不是额外之物。只是与 perquisite 拼写相近，词缀不同，意思几乎相反。

entries.definition: Something that must come first, a necessary condition. It merely shares the ending with perquisite.
entries.definitionCN: 指「先决条件」，必须先有的东西。只是与 perquisite 结尾相同，词源不同。

entries.definition: Something obtained, from quaerere, the same seeking verb, but without the prefix of "thorough".
entries.definitionCN: 指「获得的东西」，同出表示「寻求」的 quaerere，但没有「彻底」那层前缀。

entries.definition: An extra sum paid for excellent work. A bonus rewards effort, while a perquisite simply comes with the position.
entries.definitionCN: 因表现出色而额外支付的款项。bonus 奖励付出，perquisite 只是随职位附带。

entries.definition: Any advantage supplied with a job, especially health cover and pension. It is the neutral modern umbrella word.
entries.definitionCN: 工作中提供的任何好处，尤指医疗与养老金。它是现代最中性的总称。

entries.definition: A special right granted to a group or rank, close to sense 02 of perquisite.
entries.definitionCN: 授予某群体或级别的特殊权利，接近 perquisite 的第 2 个义项。

entries.definition: A benefit in addition to wages, such as a car allowance; close to the modern sense.
entries.definitionCN: 工资之外的福利，如车贴，接近现代义。

entries.definition: A fixed regular sum given for a stated purpose, narrower and more regular than a perquisite.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途定期发放的固定款项，比 perquisite 更窄、更规律。

normalIntro.en: Real parts: Latin per- "thoroughly" plus quaerere "to seek", giving perquirere and perquisitum; the clipped English form perk carries the everyday sense.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 per-「彻底」加 quaerere「寻求」，构成 perquirere 与 perquisitum；英语截短形式 perk 承担日常义。

normal.en: Quaerere means to seek, and per- means through, so a perquisite is a right sought out on top of your own.
normal.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求」，per- 意为「贯穿」，所以 perquisite 是你本分之外另去寻求的一项权利。

normal.en: Compare prerequisite, which shares the ending but means something that must come before, not extra.
normal.cn: 对比 prerequisite：结尾相同，但意思是「必须先有的东西」，不是额外的东西。

normal.en: Perquisite is legal and formal; the short perk is what people actually say, and the two are linked by years of speech.
normal.cn: perquisite 属正式、法律气味较重；日常人们说的是短的 perk，两者靠多年的口耳相传连在一起。

normal.en: The oldest sense rides with a property, the modern one rides with a post: same attaching motion.
normal.cn: 最早的义项是随财产，现代的义项是随职位：都是「附带而来」这个动作。

normal.en: In the plural, perquisites of office covers cars, seats, houses, and any advantage of rank.
normal.cn: 用复数时，perquisites of office 涵盖公车、私座、官邸等一切与级别相关的待遇。

abstract.en: Picture a wage envelope and a smaller one beside it, tied with the same string.
abstract.cn: 想象一个工资信封旁边还有一个更小的信封，用同一根绳子系着。

abstract.en: Picture a road that only members of one rank are allowed to walk, painted with the name of the office.
abstract.cn: 想象一条只允许某一级别的人行走的路，路面刷着职位名称。

abstract.en: Picture an old orchard where the tenant keeps the fruit the tree lets fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一座老果园，承租人留下树上掉下来的果实。

examples.en: The post came with the old perquisite of a hospital car.
examples.cn: 这个职位附带一项老待遇：可以用医院的公车。

examples.en: Critics argued that the perquisites of office had grown far beyond the salary.
examples.cn: 批评者认为，职务带来的各类待遇早已远远超过工资。

examples.en: In the lease, the right to gather fallen wood is stated as a perquisite.
examples.cn: 租约把捡拾落木的权利写成一项附带权利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破亏膝特」——破费又亏了膝头的特例：特殊待遇；这仅是谐音，与词源无关。

root: 源自拉丁语 perquirere「彻底寻求」（per-「彻底」加 quaerere「寻求」）的过去分词 perquisitum；核心是「另去寻得的一份额外权利或收益」；与 question、quest 同出 quaerere。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses trace one motion, something sought and claimed beyond ones own: first a right riding with a property, then with an office, then with a post, then with any job at all, and finally any advantage of rank that can be questioned.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项追踪同一个动作：超出本分之外，另去寻得并主张的东西。最初随财产一并运行，后来随官位、随职位，再后来随任何一份工作，最后是与级别相关、可能被质疑的任何好处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small second envelope tied beside the wage packet, labelled with the name of the post.
core.cn: 核心意象：工资袋旁边另系一个薄薄的小信封，上面写着职位的名字。

branches.en: EXTRA PAY: the thing given with the post on top of the wage.
branches.cn: 额外报酬：工资之外随职务发给的东西。

branches.en: RANK: what is attached to position rather than earned, praised as privilege or blamed as unfair.
branches.cn: 级别：附着于职位而并非挣来的东西，既可称为特权，也可被指为不公。

branches.en: LAW: the oldest layer, a right enjoyed beside a property.
branches.cn: 法律：最早的一层，与某项财产并列享有的权利。

branches.en: CASUAL PROFIT: the older world of fees and side income.
branches.cn: 零星收益：较早的年头里那些杂费与额外进项。

branches.en: GENERAL: any benefit a job brings, now usually the short perk.
branches.cn: 泛化：工作带来的任何好处，如今多改用短形式 perk。

intro.en: Perquisite is a latin participle turned into an English noun, and English later clipped it to the short form perk.
intro.cn: perquisite 是拉丁分词变成的英语名词，英语后来把它截短成了 perk。

latinIntro.en: The working pieces are per- "thoroughly", quaerere "to seek", and the participle ending -itum; perquirere and perquisitum explain every English form of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 可用构件是 per-「彻底」、quaerere「寻求」与分词词尾 -itum；perquirere 与 perquisitum 能解释这个词的每一个英语形式。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀说明「寻求」是彻底的。

items.example: Quaerere gives quest and question.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 衍生出 quest 与 question。

items.example: The verb names the claiming that produces a perquisite.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名了产生 perquisite 的主张动作。

items.example: The participle entered legal Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词进入了法律拉丁语。

items.meaningCN: 表示事物的名词词尾（此处指一项权利）
items.example: The ending marks the noun that English took in.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记英语借入的名词。

items.meaningCN: 截短形式，义为「额外小福利」
items.example: The short form does most of the talking.
items.exampleCN: 日常多半用这个短形式。

items.meaning: an extra benefit with a post
items.meaningCN: 随职位附带的额外福利
items.example: The full form sounds formal and legal.
items.exampleCN: 完整形式听起来正式、带法律气味。

items.example: The plural usually covers a whole package.
items.exampleCN: 复数通常指一整套待遇。

items.meaning: a privilege attached to a post
items.example: The phrase is fixed in legal and political writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个说法在法律与政治文字里已固定。
