definition_zh: 坚持不懈地；执意地；持续不断地
definition_en: in a way that keeps going or keeps happening, refusing to stop
core_image: 一个人一次次站起来，拍掉身上的土，继续往前推那扇沉重的门
scene: 凌晨的实验室里，一个人第三次重做同一个失败的实验。The young researcher persistently repeated the experiment until the reading finally made sense.
sceneCN: 这里 persistently 是「坚持不懈地」（第 1 个义项：反复做、不肯放弃地）；句意为这位年轻研究者坚持不懈地反复做实验，直到数据终于说得通。

pos.zh: 副词：坚持不懈地；执意地；持续不断地

derivatives.zh: 由 persist 加形容词后缀构成，义为「坚持的；持续的；执意的」
由拉丁语词根构成的基础动词，义为「坚持；持续存在」
由形容词词干加名词后缀构成，义为「坚持不懈；执着；持续」
persistence 的较旧同义变体，多见于医学与化学文献，指药效或性质的持久性
同义近形词，义为「坚持不懈地做下去」，词根不同，只是词义相近

senses.title: Continuing in spite of difficulty
senses.definition: in a way that keeps working at something or keeps trying, even when it is hard or has failed
senses.definitionCN: 面对困难或失败仍不断努力、不肯放弃地
senses.example: She persistently practised the piano until the piece was flawless.
senses.exampleCN: 她坚持不懈地练琴，直到那首曲子毫无瑕疵。
senses.why: The Latin prefix per- means right through, and the root means to stand firm, so a person who persists stands firm all the way to the end.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 per- 表示「一直到底」，词根表示「站稳」，所以坚持的人是把「站稳」做到终点的人。

senses.title: Repeatedly and insistently
senses.definition: in a manner that repeats an action or request again and again until someone agrees or gives in
senses.definitionCN: 一再重复某个动作或要求，直到对方同意或让步
senses.example: Reporters persistently asked the same question about the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们执意地追问同一个关于预算的问题。
senses.why: The same standing-firm image turns social: a person who will not let go keeps knocking on the same door.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「站稳不走」的画面转向社交层面：不肯放手的人会一遍遍敲同一扇门。

senses.title: Continuously over time
senses.definition: used of a condition, feeling or problem that continues for a long time and does not easily go away
senses.definitionCN: 用于指某种状况、感受或问题长久存在、不易消失地
senses.example: The region has a persistently high unemployment rate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区的失业率一直居高不下。
senses.why: If a thing keeps standing instead of falling, it shows up as a long steady condition, which is how weather and economics report trouble.
senses.whyCN: 若某事物始终保持站立而不倒下，它就会表现为长期的稳定状况，天气与经济学正是这样报告问题的。

senses.title: In a stubborn or annoying way
senses.definition: in a way that is judged stubborn, irritating or unreasonable because it will not stop
senses.definitionCN: 因不肯停止而被认为固执、烦人或不讲理地
senses.example: A wasp persisted in buzzing around the picnic table.
senses.exampleCN: 一只黄蜂在野餐桌旁不停地飞来飞去。
senses.why: Standing firm needs no good reason; when the cause is trivial, the same firmness reads as stubbornness.
senses.whyCN: 「站稳」本身不需要正当理由；当缘由微不足道时，同样的坚定就被读成固执。

senses.title: In medical descriptions
senses.definition: used of an illness, cough, pain or germ that continues or keeps returning after treatment
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容疾病、咳嗽、疼痛或病菌在治疗后仍然持续或反复出现地
senses.example: She coughed persistently for weeks after the cold.
senses.exampleCN: 感冒之后她连续咳嗽了好几个星期。
senses.why: Medicine picks up the continuing-in-time sense and narrows it to a body that will not let go of a symptom.
senses.whyCN: 医学沿用了「在时间上延续」这一层含义，并把它缩小到迟迟不放走症状的身体上。

intro.en: Persistently is built from persist, itself from Latin persistere, to keep standing firm, plus the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: persistently 由动词 persist（坚持）加副词后缀 -ly 构成；persist 来自拉丁语 persistere（站稳不倒）。

items.en: Sistere means to take a stand or stand still, and per- means right through or thoroughly.
items.cn: sistere 意为站立、站定，per- 表示「一直到底、彻底」。

items.en: Persistere combines the two: to stand firm, to continue without giving way.
items.cn: persistere 把两者合并：站稳而不退让。

items.en: The participle persistens gives the adjective persistent, with a stem persist-.
items.cn: 分词 persistens 演化为形容词 persistent，留下词干 persist-。

items.en: English borrows persist and persistent from Latin learning of the Renaissance.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的拉丁文学习把 persist 与 persistent 带进英语。

items.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into the adverb persistently, which covers steady effort and steady conditions alike.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词 persistently，同时涵盖持续的努力与持续的状况。

note.en: Persistently sits beside a small Latin family of standing-firm words and a cluster of ordinary adverbs of continuing.
note.cn: persistently 一边连着表示「站稳」的拉丁词族，一边连着表示「继续」的普通副词群。

entries.definition: continuing firmly or for a long time
to continue firmly in spite of difficulty
the quality of continuing firmly
without stopping or interruption
all the time, or again and again
in a way that refuses to change or give way

normalIntro.en: Persistently is a standing word: to persist is to stand firm all the way, and the adverb lets that firmness qualify a whole action.
normalIntro.cn: persistently 是一个「站立」的词：persist 就是一路站稳，副词则让这种坚守去修饰整个动作。

normal.en: Persistently = persistent + ly: the adjective turns into an adverb of manner.
normal.cn: persistently 等于 persistent 加 ly：形容词变成方式副词。

normal.en: Keep the word family together: persist, persistent, persistence, persistently.
normal.cn: 把词族放在一起记：persist、persistent、persistence、persistently。

normal.en: In IELTS writing, persistently often describes a trend, as in a persistently high rate.
normal.cn: 在雅思写作中，persistently 常用来描述趋势，如「持续偏高的比率」。

normal.en: In speaking, persistently describes effort, as in persisting with a task.
normal.cn: 在口语中，persistently 常用来描述努力，如「坚持做一项任务」。

normal.en: Compare insistently: persistently stresses a standing effort, insistently stresses pressing a demand.
normal.cn: 对比 insistently：persistently 强调稳住努力，insistently 强调紧逼要求。

abstract.en: Picture a climber who slips twice on the cliff and sets a hand on the rock a third time.
abstract.cn: 想象一名攀登者在崖壁上滑落两次，第三次又把手搭上岩石。

abstract.en: Hear a repeated knock at a door: patient the first time, harder the tenth.
abstract.cn: 听那一下下的敲门声：第一次还算耐心，第十次就重了。

abstract.en: Watch a line on a chart that refuses to dip: that flat line is a persistently high figure.
abstract.cn: 看图表上那条迟迟不肯下落的线：那条平线就是「持续偏高」的数字。

examples.en: She persistently pursued the right answer, even after three dead ends.
examples.cn: 即使在三次走进死胡同之后，她仍坚持不懈地追寻正确答案。

examples.en: Parents are often persistently anxious about their children and social media.
examples.cn: 父母常常持续不断地为孩子的社交媒体使用而焦虑。

examples.en: The medicine had a persistently unpleasant taste.
examples.cn: 这种药的味道一直让人不太舒服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕死他」——怕死也要站稳不走，就是坚持不懈；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（一直到底）+ sistere（站立、站定）→ persistere（站稳不退）→ 英语 persist（坚持）+ -ent（形容词）→ persistent + -ly（副词）→ persistently，核心义「一直站住」。

sensesIntro.en: Persistently starts from a concrete standing firm, extends into insisting on a request, then into a long-lasting condition, and finally into stubbornness and medical persistence.
sensesIntro.cn: persistently 从具体的「站稳不退」出发，扩展到一再提出要求，再扩展到长期存在的状况，最后落到固执与医学上的缠绵不愈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone slips, gets up, and keeps pushing the heavy door.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人跌倒、爬起，继续去推那扇沉重的门。

branches.en: The body sense: effort continues against difficulty.
branches.cn: 身体线：努力在困难中持续下去。

branches.en: The social sense: the same firmness presses other people.
branches.cn: 社交线：同样的坚定作用在别人身上。

branches.en: The time sense: conditions and symptoms that will not fall down stay on.
branches.cn: 时间线：不倒下的状况与症状会一直延续。

branches.en: The attitude sense: firmness without a good reason reads as stubbornness.
branches.cn: 态度线：没有正当理由的坚定被读成固执。

branches.en: Both the worker and the reporter are holding on to the same stance while others let go.
branches.cn: 无论是工作者还是记者，都在别人松手时保持同一个站姿。

intro.en: Persistently is a Latin base plus two English layering steps: an adjective ending and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: persistently 由拉丁语词根加两层英语后缀构成：先加形容词词尾，再加副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere and persistere are recorded, and the deeper Indo-European stem is reconstructed rather than directly attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere 与 persistere 均有文献记录，更早的印欧词干则属于重构形式。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of carrying on to the end.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「坚持到最后」的意思。

items.meaning: to stand, to take a stand
items.example: The verb supplies the standing image of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为这个词提供「站立」的意象。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of English persist.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语 persist 的直接来源。

items.example: Persist is the basic English verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: persist 是这一词族的基础英语动词。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into persistent.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成 persistent。

items.example: Persistent describes a person or a condition that holds on.
items.exampleCN: persistent 描述坚持不放的人或状况。

items.example: The suffix builds persistence from the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀用形容词词干构成 persistence。

items.example: The suffix turns persistent into persistently.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 persistent 变成 persistently。

items.example: Persistence is the noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: persistence 是这一词族的名词。

latinEntries.meaning: to stand, to take a stand

definition_zh: 使个性化；使适合特定个人；为个人定制；在（物品）上标出姓名
definition_en: to change an object, service or message so that it matches one particular person, or to mark something with the name of that person
core_image: 流水线上的标准式样，被一双手贴上写着自己名字的标签
scene: 新开的咖啡馆里，店员在杯子上写下顾客的名字。The barista personalizes each cup so that every regular finds their own name waiting at the counter.
sceneCN: 这里 personalize 是「为个人定制」（第 1 个义项：按某个人的特点或需求加以调整）；句意为咖啡师对每只杯子做个性化处理，让每位常客都能在柜台找到写着自己名字的那杯。

pos.zh: 使个性化；为个人定制；按个人需求调整
在物品上标出姓名或标记

derivatives.zh: 由 person 加形容词后缀构成，本词即在它基础上加动词后缀而来
由 personal 加副词后缀构成，义为「亲自；就个人而言」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「个性化；个性化定制」
同根名词，义为「个性；人格；名人」，与个性化同源但语义已分化
最基础的同源名词，义为「人；个人」

senses.title: To adapt something to one person
senses.titleCN: 使个性化；为特定个人调整
senses.definition: to change a product, service, message or experience so that it suits one particular person rather than everyone
senses.definitionCN: 改变产品、服务、信息或体验，使其适合某个特定的人而非所有人
senses.example: The app personalizes your news feed by tracking what you read.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用通过记录你阅读的内容来个性化你的新闻推送。
senses.why: Person is in the middle of the word, so to personalize is to bend a general thing into the shape of one person.
senses.whyCN: person 就嵌在这个词的中央，所以 personalize 就是把一件通用的东西弯成某一个人的形状。

senses.title: To mark something with a name
senses.definition: to put the name, initials or photograph of a person on an object such as a cup, bag or book
senses.definitionCN: 把某人的姓名、首字母或照片印在杯子、包、书本等物品上
senses.example: She personalized the notebooks with our initials.
senses.exampleCN: 她在笔记本上印了我们的姓名首字母。
senses.why: The most literal way to make a thing belong to a person is to write that person on it.
senses.whyCN: 让一件东西属于某个人，最直接的办法就是把这个人的名字写在上面。

senses.title: To present as personal
senses.titleCN: 使带个人色彩；针对个人而言
senses.definition: to express an idea or attack in a way aimed at a particular individual rather than at a general question
senses.definitionCN: 以针对某个具体个人的方式表达观点或发起攻击，而非针对一般问题
senses.example: Try not to personalize the criticism; it is about the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 尽量不要把批评当作针对个人的；它针对的是计划本身。
senses.why: When a neutral remark is turned on a single person, the issue has been dragged into the personal sphere.
senses.whyCN: 当一句中性的评论被转向某个人时，问题就被拖进了「个人」的领域。

senses.title: To treat as belonging to one person
senses.titleCN: 使归属个人；视作某人专有
senses.definition: to take something shared and make it feel or become the property of a private individual
senses.definitionCN: 把共有的东西变成或被视为某个私人个体的所有物
senses.example: The new tenants personalized the shared garden with their own benches.
senses.exampleCN: 新住户用自己的长椅把公共花园变成了私人天地。
senses.why: Ownership is the other face of the same move: what belongs to one person looks marked by that person.
senses.whyCN: 归属是同一动作的另一面：属于某个人的东西，看上去就带着那个人的印记。

senses.title: In computer systems
senses.titleCN: （计）个性化设置；按用户喜好配置
senses.definition: used of software and websites that let a user change settings, layout or content to their own taste
senses.definitionCN: 用于软件和网站，让用户按自己的喜好更改设置、布局或内容
senses.example: You can personalize the browser with themes and quick links.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以用主题和快捷链接来个性化你的浏览器。
senses.why: Computing simply automates the adaptation: the system learns each user and reshapes itself for that one account.
senses.whyCN: 计算机只是把这种调整自动化了：系统了解每位用户，并为那一个账户重新塑形。

intro.en: Personalize is built from person, through the adjective personal, plus the verb suffix -ize, which entered English with the Latin termination -izare.
intro.cn: personalize 由 person（人）出发，经由形容词 personal，再加上来自拉丁语 -izare 的动词后缀 -ize 构成。

items.en: Persona is first a mask worn by an actor, and later a role or an individual in law.
items.cn: persona 最初指演员戴的面具，后来指角色，并在法律上指个人。

items.en: Old French persone and Latin persona reach English as person, a human being or an individual.
items.cn: 古法语 persone 与拉丁语 persona 进入英语成为 person，指人或个体。

items.en: The adjective personalis means belonging to a person, and English personal carries that meaning.
items.cn: 形容词 personalis 表示「属于个人的」，英语 personal 沿用了这个意思。

items.en: The suffix -ize comes from Greek -izein through Latin -izare and French -iser; it makes verbs from nouns and adjectives.
items.cn: 后缀 -ize 经希腊语 -izein、拉丁语 -izare 与法语 -iser 传来，用来把名词和形容词变作动词。

items.en: Earlier spellings such as personalise follow the French path; the form personalize belongs to the period when English verbs took -ize more freely.
items.cn: 较早的拼法 personalise 走的是法语一路，personalize 这一形式则出现于英语动词普遍采用 -ize 的时期。

items.en: The verb shifts from marking a possession to adapting a service, and then to the data-driven tailoring of the internet age.
items.cn: 这个动词由标出所有物，转向调整服务，再转向互联网时代由数据驱动的量身定制。

note.en: Personalize is a make-a-verb from the person family; its neighbours are the family itself and the wider set of customising words.
note.cn: personalize 是由 person 词族造出的动词；它的邻词既有同族成员，也有更宽的一组「定制」类词。

entries.definition: belonging to or affecting one person
in person, or as far as I am concerned
the act of making something fit one person
to change something to suit a customer or user
entries.definitionCN: 按客户或用户的需要定制

entries.definition: to make or adapt something for a particular purpose or person
entries.definitionCN: 量身定制；使适应特定用途

entries.definition: to make something individual and distinct from the rest
entries.definitionCN: 使个体化；使具有个体特色

normalIntro.en: Personalize wears its root openly: person sits in the middle, -al makes the adjective, and -ize makes the verb meaning to make things personal.
normalIntro.cn: personalize 把词根明明白白地摆在中间：person 在正中，-al 使它成为形容词，-ize 再把它变成「使……个人化」的动词。

normal.en: Remember the chain person, personal, personalize, personalization, and the pattern is easy to see.
normal.cn: 记住 person、personal、personalize、personalization 这串词，构词规律就一目了然。

normal.en: British English prefers personalise, while American English prefers personalize.
normal.cn: 英式英语多用 personalise，美式英语多用 personalize。

normal.en: In IELTS speaking, describe how shops and apps tailor services to one buyer.
normal.cn: 在雅思口语中，可以描述商店和应用如何为某一个买家量身定制服务。

normal.en: In reading texts, personalized medicine and personalized learning are common technical collocations.
normal.cn: 在阅读文章里，个体化医疗与个性化学习是常见的技术性搭配。

normal.en: Compare personalize with customize: personalize puts a person at the centre, customize puts an order at the centre.
normal.cn: 对比 personalize 与 customize：personalize 以「人」为中心，customize 以「订单」为中心。

abstract.en: Picture a cup stamped with a name that is not yours, then one stamped with yours.
abstract.cn: 想象一只印着别人名字的杯子，再换一只印着你名字的杯子。

abstract.en: Think of a machine cutting a paper tag into the outline of a small face.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器把纸标签裁成一张小脸的轮廓。

abstract.en: Imagine a website that changes its look the moment a different login appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一个网站，在另一个账号登录的瞬间就换了一副样子。

examples.en: The school personalizes lessons for pupils who learn at different speeds.
examples.cn: 这所学校为学习速度不同的学生量身定制课程。

examples.en: Her parents had personalized the photo album with our names on every page.
examples.cn: 她的父母把相册做了个性化处理，每一页都写着我们的名字。

examples.en: Social platforms personalize what each user sees, which narrows the range of opinions.
examples.cn: 社交平台为每个用户定制所见内容，这会收窄他们接触观点的范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破森那来子」——破森也要给每个人配一份，就是个性化定制；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 persona（面具；角色；个人）→ person（人）+ -al（形容词后缀）→ personal（个人的）+ -ize（动词后缀）→ personalize（使个人化），核心义「把通用的东西变成某个人自己的」。

sensesIntro.en: Personalize begins with adapting a thing to one person, then marking it with that person own name, then turning remarks toward a person, then giving it into one person own hands, and finally letting software do it automatically.
sensesIntro.cn: personalize 先指把东西调整到适合某一人，再指在上面写上那人的名字，又指把话说向某一人，接着指把它交到某一人手中，最后让软件自动完成这一步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a standard object gets a tag with one name on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：标准化的物件被贴上一张写着某个人名字的标签。

branches.en: The service sense: a general product is bent to one person.
branches.cn: 服务线：通用的产品被弯成某个人的形状。

branches.en: The object sense: a name is written on a thing to claim it.
branches.cn: 物件线：把名字写在东西上以宣示归属。

branches.en: The social sense: remarks and shared things are pulled into one person sphere.
branches.cn: 社交线：话语与共有之物被拉进某个人的领域。

branches.en: The digital sense: software repeats the same adaptation at scale.
branches.cn: 数字线：软件把同一种调整规模化地重复。

branches.en: A personalized feed is the tailor image run by a machine account by account.
branches.cn: 个性化推送就是让机器逐个账户地执行「裁缝」这一意象。

intro.en: Personalize is built from a Latin noun, an adjective ending and a Greek-Latin verb ending, so every piece is traceable.
intro.cn: personalize 由一个拉丁名词、一个形容词词尾和一个希腊拉丁通用的动词词尾构成，每一部分都可以追到源头。

latinIntro.en: Latin persona and personalis are recorded, while the verb suffix -izare came into Latin from Greek and then into English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 persona 与 personalis 均有文献记录；动词词尾 -izare 由希腊语进入拉丁语，再经法语进入英语。

items.example: Persona is the source noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: persona 是整个词族背后的源名词。

items.example: Person is the everyday base of the word.
items.exampleCN: person 是这个词最日常的基础。

items.example: The suffix turns person into personal.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 person 变成 personal。

items.example: Personal is the adjective the verb is built on.
items.exampleCN: personal 是这个动词所依附的形容词。

items.example: The suffix makes a verb out of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成动词。

items.meaningCN: 受法语影响的英式拼法
items.example: The variant appears in British English as personalise.
items.exampleCN: 这个变体在英式英语中写作 personalise。

items.example: The suffix builds personalization.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 personalization。

items.example: The suffix builds personality from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀用同一词根构成 personality。

items.meaningCN: 个性化的；按个人定制的
items.example: Personalized describes the finished result.
items.exampleCN: personalized 描述完成之后的结果。

latinEntries.meaning: the quality of being an individual

definition_zh: 敏锐的；有洞察力的；明察秋毫的
definition_en: quick to notice and understand things that others miss, especially hidden motives or coming problems
core_image: 一双眼睛穿过浓雾，一眼看清远处那条还没人走的小路
scene: 年长的会计师对异常数字一向格外敏感，可这一次她只说了一句，没人当真。The chief accountant, a famously perspicacious pair of eyes, summed up the figures in one quiet remark.
sceneCN: 这里 perspicacious 是「很有洞察力的」（第 1 个义项：能敏锐看出别人没注意到的东西）；句意为只有最有洞察力的审计师在崩盘之前看出了账目中的漏洞。

pos.zh: 敏锐的；有洞察力的；有远见的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「洞察力；敏锐；洞悉力」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「敏锐地；有洞察力地」
同根近形词，义为「表达清楚易懂的」，注意后缀不同，词义偏向「清晰」

senses.title: Keen and discerning
senses.definition: having a quick and sharp mind that notices and understands things which are not obvious
senses.definitionCN: 头脑敏锐，能注意到并理解并不明显的事物
senses.example: Her perspicacious reading of the report saved the company a fortune.
senses.exampleCN: 她对报告的敏锐解读为公司省下了一大笔钱。
senses.why: Latin perspicere means to see through, and the compound literally joins seeing with seeing through something, so the adjective names the mind that sees through.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 perspicere 意为「看穿」，这个词的复合结构把「看」和「看透」合在一起，因此这个形容词指的就是能看穿的头脑。

senses.title: Foreseeing what will follow
senses.definition: able to judge what is going to happen before other people notice the signs
senses.definitionCN: 在别人察觉迹象之前就能判断将会发生什么
senses.example: A perspicacious investor sold before the market turned.
senses.exampleCN: 一位有先见之明的投资者在市场转向之前就已卖出。
senses.why: Seeing through fog is not only about what stands there now, but also about the road that is about to appear.
senses.whyCN: 看穿浓雾，不只是看清此刻立着的东西，也看得到即将出现的那条路。

senses.title: Seeing through people
senses.definition: quick to see the true character or hidden motive behind what a person says or shows
senses.definitionCN: 能迅速看穿一个人说辞或表象背后的真实品性、隐藏动机
senses.example: He was too perspicacious to be fooled by the charming gesture.
senses.exampleCN: 他太有洞察力了，不会被人那副讨喜的姿态骗到。
senses.why: The same seeing-through becomes social: another person is a surface, and the discerning mind reads what is behind it.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「看穿」转向了人际：他人的表现是一层表面，敏锐的头脑读到的是表面之后的东西。

senses.title: In formal or literary writing
senses.definition: used in formal and literary prose of a remark, book or argument that shows deep and clear understanding
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或文学性的文字中形容评论、书籍或论述体现出深刻而清晰的理解
senses.example: The essay offers a perspicacious account of the war debt.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章对战债做了十分深刻清晰的论述。
senses.why: Because the word is Latin and long, it grows a formal register that suits analysis and criticism more than chat.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词来自拉丁语且偏长，它自然长出了一层正式语域，更适合分析与批评而不适合闲聊。

senses.title: Distinguishing the lookalikes
senses.titleCN: 区别于 perspicuous 的「洞察」义
senses.definition: used chiefly of a person judgment, in contrast with perspicuous, which describes a text or speech as clear
senses.definitionCN: 主要形容人的判断力，而与形容文字、言辞清晰易懂的 perspicuous 相对
senses.example: The critic was perspicacious, but her prose was barely perspicuous.
senses.exampleCN: 这位评论家很有洞察力，但她的文章却几乎读不懂。
senses.why: Both adjectives come from the same seeing root, yet one ended up about a sharp mind and the other about a clear style.
senses.whyCN: 这两个形容词出自同一个表示「看」的词根，但一个落在了「心思敏锐」上，另一个落在了「文风清晰」上。

intro.en: Perspicacious comes from Latin perspicere, to look through, whose roots are per-, through, and specere, to look.
intro.cn: perspicacious 来自拉丁语 perspicere（看穿），其词根是 per-（穿过）与 specere（看）。

items.en: A reconstructed root spek- underlies many words for looking; the depth beyond this is uncertain.
items.cn: 一个重构词根 spek- 是许多表示「看」的词的基础，比这更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Specere means to look or watch, and appears in words such as aspect and inspect.
items.cn: specere 意为看、注视，并出现在 aspect、inspect 等词中。

items.en: Perspicere joins per-, through, with specere, so it means to see through a thing.
items.cn: perspicere 把表示「穿过」的 per- 与 specere 合起来，于是意为看透某物。

items.en: The adjective perspicax, with stem perspicac-, means sharp-sighted and is the direct parent of the English word.
items.cn: 形容词 perspicax（词干 perspicac-）意为目光锐利，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: The French form perspicace, or the Latin stem itself, reaches English as perspicacious.
items.cn: 法语形式 perspicace 或拉丁词干本身进入英语，成为 perspicacious。

items.en: The noun perspicacity now spans sharp judgment, insight into people and foresight.
items.cn: 名词 perspicacity 如今涵盖敏锐判断、识人与先见之明。

note.en: Perspicacious belongs to the Latin seeing family; its lookalikes are built from the same spectator root, and its near meanings are the ordinary words for sharpness of mind.
note.cn: perspicacious 属于拉丁语「看」的词族；形近词都出自同一「观看」词根，近义词则是表示头脑敏锐的常用词。

entries.definition: the quality of seeing clearly and judging sharply
clearly expressed and easy to understand
entries.definitionCN: 表达清楚的；易懂的（后缀不同，义偏清晰，非「敏锐」）

entries.definition: looking into your own thoughts and feelings
entries.definitionCN: 内省；自我审视（同源「看」词根）

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand things
good at noticing details
clever at judging situations and people, often for practical gain
entries.definitionCN: 精明的；判断敏锐的（常带算计意味）

normalIntro.en: Perspicacious is a seeing word: per- through, spec- look, plus the adjective ending -acious, so it means looking right through a thing.
normalIntro.cn: perspicacious 是一个「看」的词：per- 表示穿透，spec- 表示看，再加形容词词尾 -acious，合起来就是一眼看穿。

normal.en: Keep the family together: perspicacious, perspicacity, perspicuously, perspicuous.
normal.cn: 把词族放在一起记：perspicacious、perspicacity、perspicuously、perspicuous。

normal.en: The root spec- also appears in inspect, respect and spectator, all about looking.
normal.cn: 词根 spec- 也出现在 inspect、respect 与 spectator 里，都与「看」有关。

normal.en: Do not confuse perspicacious with perspicuous: sharp mind versus clear style.
normal.cn: 不要把 perspicacious 和 perspicuous 搞混：前者是头脑敏锐，后者是表达清晰。

normal.en: The word is formal, so use it in writing about analysis, criticism or judgment.
normal.cn: 这个词很正式，宜用于关于分析、批评与判断的书面表达。

normal.en: Compare perceptive, which is the everyday cousin of the same meaning.
normal.cn: 对比 perceptive：它是同义里更日常的那一个。

abstract.en: Picture a lighthouse beam cutting straight through fog to a boat no one else has seen.
abstract.cn: 想象一束灯塔光笔直穿过浓雾，照到一条别人都没看见的船。

abstract.en: Imagine a detective who reads a room and names the missing chair at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一位侦探扫视一间屋子，立刻说出少了哪把椅子。

abstract.en: Think of a chess player who sees three moves ahead while others see only the board.
abstract.cn: 想象一位棋手已经看到三步之后，而别人只看见眼前的棋盘。

examples.en: Her perspicacious questions forced the committee to admit the flaw.
examples.cn: 她那些敏锐的问题迫使委员会承认了漏洞。

examples.en: The novel offers a perspicacious portrait of provincial ambition.
examples.cn: 这部小说对外省人的野心作了十分深刻的描绘。

examples.en: A perspicacious merchant noticed the demand before any rival did.
examples.cn: 一位有洞察力的商人比任何对手都更早注意到了这一需求。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破斯皮看啥斯」——拨开皮仔细看的是啥，一眼看穿，就是敏锐；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（穿过、彻底）+ specere（看）→ perspicere（看穿）→ 形容词 perspicax（词干 perspicac-，目光锐利）→ 英语 perspicacious，核心义「一眼看透」。

sensesIntro.en: Perspicacious starts from a sharp, seeing mind, extends to foresight and to reading people, settles into a formal written register, and is usually distinguished from its lookalike perspicuous.
sensesIntro.cn: perspicacious 先从「目光锐利的头脑」出发，延伸到先见之明与识人，再落定在正式的书面语域，且常与形近的 perspicuous 相区分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye that cuts through fog and finds the hidden path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只眼睛穿过浓雾，找到那条隐藏的小路。

branches.en: The mind sense: sharp noticing is the everyday meaning.
branches.cn: 心智线：敏锐察觉是最核心的含义。

branches.en: The time sense: seeing through extends forward into prediction.
branches.cn: 时间线：看穿延伸到对未来的预判。

branches.en: The people sense: a person is a surface to be read.
branches.cn: 人际线：人本身是一层需要被读懂的表面。

branches.en: The register sense: the Latin length gives the word a formal written place.
branches.cn: 语域线：拉丁词形偏长，使它在正式书面语中占一席之地。

branches.en: The same root became one word for a sharp mind and one for a clear style.
branches.cn: 同一词根分出一个表示头脑敏锐的词和一个表示文风清晰的词。

intro.en: Perspicacious is assembled from a Latin prefix, a Latin seeing root, and an adjective ending borrowed through Latin and French.
intro.cn: perspicacious 由拉丁语前缀、表示「看」的拉丁词根，以及经拉丁语和法语传来的形容词词尾拼成。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere and perspicere are recorded, while the older verb perspicare reported in the dictionaries is rare and its use is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere 与 perspicere 均有文献记录；词典所收更早的动词 perspicare 极为罕见，其使用情况存在不确定。

items.example: The prefix gives the idea of looking all the way through.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀带来「一路看穿」的意思。

items.example: The root also appears in inspect and spectator.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也出现在 inspect 与 spectator 里。

items.example: The verb is the core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这个词族的核心。

items.meaning: to see through, to see clearly
items.example: Perspicere is the direct parent of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: perspicere 是这个形容词的直接来源。

items.example: The Latin adjective supplies the perspicac- stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词提供了 perspicac- 这一词干。

items.example: The suffix turns the stem into an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成英语形容词。

items.example: The suffix builds perspicacity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 perspicacity。

items.example: The suffix builds perspicaciously.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 perspicaciously。

items.example: The variant suffix builds perspicuous, which means clear rather than sharp.
items.exampleCN: 这一变体词尾构成 perspicuous，指表达清晰而非头脑敏锐。

latinEntries.meaning: to see through, to see clearly

definition_zh: 出汗；流汗；渗出水汽
definition_en: to produce sweat through the tiny pores of the skin
core_image: 皮肤上的小孔正向外面呼出一层细细的水汽
scene: 跑完最后一圈，选手的额头早已全是汗水。After the final lap, the runner began to perspire heavily.
sceneCN: 这里 perspire 是「出汗」（第 1 个义项：皮肤通过毛孔排出汗水）；句意：跑完最后一圈，选手开始大量出汗。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「汗水；出汗」
由名词加 -ory 构成，义为「汗腺的；与出汗有关的」
加 -able 构成，义为「可汗出的；可通过毛孔排出的」

senses.title: To give off sweat through the skin
senses.definition: to release sweat through the pores of the skin, especially when hot or nervous
senses.definitionCN: 在炎热或紧张时通过皮肤毛孔排出汗水
senses.example: Climbers perspire a great deal on the steep path.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者在陡峭的小路上出很多汗。
senses.why: The Latin prefix per- carries the idea of through, and spirare means to breathe, so the skin is pictured breathing out moisture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 per- 表示「穿过」，spirare 意为「呼吸」，所以皮肤被想象成在向外呼出水汽，这就是最基础的出汗义。

senses.title: To sweat from effort or emotion
senses.definition: to sweat because of physical effort, heat, or strong feeling rather than disease
senses.definitionCN: 因体力活动、炎热或强烈情绪而冒汗，而非因病
senses.example: He perspired with nerves before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前他紧张得冒汗。
senses.why: Since sweat is released through the skin, the same verb covers sweating driven by effort, heat, or emotion.
senses.whyCN: 既然汗水是从皮肤透出来的，这同一个动词也涵盖由劳累、炎热或情绪引发的冒汗。

senses.title: To ooze out like sweat
senses.definition: of a liquid, to come out slowly through a surface as if through pores
senses.definitionCN: 液体像汗水一样从表面缓慢渗出
senses.example: Cold water perspires on the outside of the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 冷水在玻璃杯外壁凝成水珠，像渗出来一样。
senses.why: The picture of moisture breathing out of tiny holes extends from the body to any surface that leaks slowly.
senses.whyCN: 水汽从小孔向外呼出的画面，从身体延伸到任何缓慢渗水的表面。

intro.en: Perspire comes from Latin perspirare, to breathe through, from per-, through, and spirare, to breathe.
intro.cn: perspire 来自拉丁语 perspirare（透过呼吸），由 per-（穿过）与 spirare（呼吸）组成。

items.en: Spirare means to breathe, and spiritus means breath.
items.cn: spirare 意为呼吸，spiritus 意为气息。

items.en: Perspirare means to breathe through or transpire, used of pores letting vapour out.
items.cn: perspirare 意为透过呼吸、蒸发，用于毛孔向外排出水汽。

items.en: French perspirer carries the medical sense of sweating through the skin.
items.cn: 法语 perspirer 把透过皮肤出汗的医学含义带入近代欧洲语言。

items.en: English perspire first names invisible sweat leaving the body in medical writing.
items.cn: 英语 perspire 先在医学文献中指身体排出的不可见汗气。

items.en: Everyday English widens perspire to any visible sweating, and adds the sense of liquid oozing from a surface.
items.cn: 现代英语把 perspire 扩大到任何可见的出汗，并增加液体从表面渗出的义项。

note.en: Perspire sits beside its Latin relatives inspired and respire, and near the everyday sweaty words.
note.cn: perspire 与同根的 inspired、respire 相邻，也与日常的「出汗」类词近义。

entries.definition: sweat, or the act of sweating
to give off vapour through the surface, or to become known
entries.definitionCN: 表面蒸发（尤指植物散失水分）；后来指事情泄露、为人所知

entries.definition: to breathe
to breathe in, or to fill someone with a feeling or idea
to produce sweat, the common everyday verb
to be very hot and uncomfortable
to flow out slowly from something

normalIntro.en: Perspire carries the Latin verb to breathe: the body breathes moisture out through its pores.
normalIntro.cn: perspire 带着拉丁语「呼吸」的动词：身体通过毛孔把水汽呼出去。

normal.en: To perspire is to sweat, a formal word for the everyday sweat.
normal.cn: perspire 就是出汗，是 sweat 的正式说法。

normal.en: Perspiration is the noun for sweat, as in beads of perspiration.
normal.cn: perspiration 是「汗水」的名词，如 beads of perspiration 汗珠。

normal.en: Per- means through, and spirare means to breathe, so perspire is to breathe through the skin.
normal.cn: per- 表示穿过，spirare 表示呼吸，所以 perspire 就是透过皮肤呼吸。

normal.en: Compare transpire: plants transpire water, animals perspire sweat.
normal.cn: 对比 transpire：植物散发水汽，动物排出汗水；两词共享「蒸发」意象。

normal.en: Doctors may say a patient perspires, a softer way to report sweating.
normal.cn: 医生会说病人 perspires，这是比「冒汗」更委婉的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a runner whose forehead is covered in fine drops.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者额头布满细密的水珠。

abstract.en: Imagine a nervous speaker wiping a hand on the trousers.
abstract.cn: 想象紧张的演讲者在裤子上擦手。

abstract.en: Think of a cold glass leaking tiny drops onto the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只冰杯在桌上渗出小水珠。

examples.en: Athletes perspire heavily during a long race.
examples.cn: 运动员在长跑中大量出汗。

examples.en: She perspired with fear as the lift stopped.
examples.cn: 电梯停下时，她害怕得直冒汗。

examples.en: Water perspires on the cold surface of the pipe.
examples.cn: 管道冰冷的表面会渗出小水珠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕死鼻涕」——吓得怕死、鼻涕直冒，正好记出汗；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（穿过）+ spirare（呼吸）→ perspirare（透过呼吸）→ 法语 perspirer → 英语 perspire，核心义「透过皮肤呼出水汽」。

sensesIntro.en: Perspire begins with sweat leaving the body, then covers sweating from effort and emotion, and finally widens to liquid oozing from a surface.
sensesIntro.cn: perspire 先指汗水离开身体，再覆盖劳累与情绪引发的冒汗，最后扩大到液体从表面渗出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tiny pores breathing out a fine mist of water.
core.cn: 核心意象：皮肤上的小孔向外呼出一层细细的水汽。

branches.en: The basic sense is sweat released through pores.
branches.cn: 基本义是通过毛孔排出汗水。

branches.en: Effort and emotion become common triggers of sweating.
branches.cn: 劳累与情绪成为出汗的常见诱因。

branches.en: Slow leaking liquid extends the pore image to surfaces.
branches.cn: 缓慢渗出的液体把毛孔意象延伸到各种表面。

branches.en: Both the body and a cold glass let moisture out slowly.
branches.cn: 身体与冰凉杯壁都缓慢放出水汽。

branches.en: Nervous sweating is still ordinary sweating, only with a different cause.
branches.cn: 紧张的冒汗仍是普通出汗，只是原因不同。

intro.en: Perspire is built from the Latin prefix per- and the root spir-, which also gives spirit, inspire, and respire.
intro.cn: perspire 由拉丁语前缀 per- 与词根 spir- 构成，同一词根还给出 spirit、inspire 与 respire。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare means to breathe, and per- means through, so perspirare means to breathe through.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spirare 意为呼吸，per- 意为穿过，perspirare 即透过呼吸。

items.example: The prefix per- marks movement through.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 per- 标记「穿过」的方向。

items.example: The root spir- appears in many breathing words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 spir- 出现在许多与呼吸有关的词中。

items.example: Spirare is the direct verb source.
items.exampleCN: spirare 是直接动词来源。

items.example: Perspirare joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: perspirare 把前缀与词根连接起来。

items.meaningCN: 行为或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms perspiration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 perspiration。

items.example: Perspiration is the common noun form.
items.exampleCN: perspiration 是最常见的名词形式。

items.example: Transpire shares the root and adds trans-.
items.exampleCN: transpire 共享词根并加上前缀 trans-。

items.example: Respire is the plain breathing relative.
items.exampleCN: respire 是最朴素的「呼吸」同源词。

items.example: Inspire shows how the root moved from air to feeling.
items.exampleCN: inspire 展示词根如何从气息转向感受。

definition_zh: 相关的；切题的；中肯的
definition_en: closely connected with the matter being discussed and therefore worth saying
core_image: 一支箭不偏不倚，正好落在讨论的正中
scene: 会议讨论预算，有人却讲起去年的天气，这显然不切题。In the budget meeting, the chair asked for comments that were pertinent to the figures.
sceneCN: 这里 pertinent 是「切题的」（第 1 个义项：与正在讨论的事情直接相关）；句意：在预算会议上，主持人请大家只谈与数字相关的意见。

collocations.zh: 切题的问题；中肯的提问

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ence 构成，义为「相关性；切题」
同义名词形式，义为「相关性；中肯」
加否定前缀 im- 构成，字面是「不相干的」，常转指「无礼的、不敬的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「切题地；中肯地」

senses.title: Directly connected with the topic
senses.definition: closely related to the subject that is being discussed or considered
senses.definitionCN: 与正在讨论或考虑的主题密切相关的
senses.example: The lawyer asked several pertinent questions.
senses.exampleCN: 律师问了几个切题的问题。
senses.why: The Latin verb pertinere means to stretch toward or belong to, so a pertinent remark reaches toward the topic at hand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 pertinere 意为「伸向、属于」，所以 pertinent 的言论会伸向眼下的话题，因而直接相关。

senses.title: Worth saying for the matter
senses.definition: relevant in a way that matters and helps the matter being dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 相关性重要且有助于处理当前问题
senses.example: Her point about cost was pertinent to the whole plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她关于成本的看法对整个计划都很重要。
senses.why: If something belongs to the problem, it is not merely related but useful, so the sense shades into important and helpful.
senses.whyCN: 如果某事属于这个问题本身，那它就不只是相关，还很有用，因此义项转成「重要、有益」。

senses.title: To the point, not rambling
senses.titleCN: 中肯的；直接切中要害的
senses.definition: expressed briefly and exactly on the point, without wandering away
senses.definitionCN: 简短准确地落在要点上，不东拉西扯
senses.example: His pertinent comment ended the long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句中肯的评论结束了冗长的争论。
senses.why: Because the word describes what belongs to the point, it also praises speech that stays on the point and cuts away the rest.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词描述的是「属于要点」的东西，它也用来称赞不跑题的发言，即直接切中要害。

intro.en: Pertinent comes from Latin pertinere, to reach or belong, from per-, thoroughly, and tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: pertinent 来自拉丁语 pertinere（伸向、属于），由 per-（彻底）与 tenere（握住）构成。

items.en: Tenere means to hold, and gives English tenant and contain.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住，英语的 tenant、contain 都由它而来。

items.en: Pertinere means to stretch toward, to reach, or to belong to.
items.cn: pertinere 意为伸向、触及或属于。

items.en: Pertinens, belonging to a thing, is used in legal and scholarly Latin.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 pertinens 表示「属于某事的」，常用于法律与学术文本。

items.en: English pertinent first means appertaining or belonging to a person or matter.
items.cn: 英语 pertinent 最初表示「属于某人或某事」。

items.en: The sense narrows to relating to the point and hence to being topical and to the point.
items.cn: 现代英语中意义收窄为「与要点相关」，进而指「切题的、中肯的」。

note.en: Pertinent shares the Latin holding root with appertain and contain, and stands near relevant and applicable in meaning.
note.cn: pertinent 与 appertain、contain 共享拉丁语「握住」词根，在意义上靠近 relevant 与 applicable。

entries.definition: the quality of being relevant
rude, or not relevant to the matter
to belong to as a part
to hold inside
connected with what is being discussed or done
able to be applied to a case or situation
closely connected and suitable to the subject

normalIntro.en: Pertinent holds the idea of reaching toward: whatever belongs to the topic reaches it.
normalIntro.cn: pertinent 带有「伸向」的意思：凡是属于话题的东西都会伸向它。

normal.en: Something pertinent is relevant to the question being asked.
normal.cn: pertinent 的事物就是与所问问题相关的事物。

normal.en: Pertinent to is the most common pattern, as in facts pertinent to the case.
normal.cn: pertinent to 是最常见的搭配，如 facts pertinent to the case。

normal.en: Pertinence is the noun, naming the quality of being relevant.
normal.cn: pertinence 是名词，指相关的性质。

normal.en: Impertinent adds a negative prefix, so the literal meaning is not belonging, and it often means rude.
normal.cn: impertinent 加上否定前缀，字面是「不属于」，常指「无礼」。

normal.en: Compare relevant: relevant is the everyday word, pertinent is more formal and suggests wisdom.
normal.cn: 对比 relevant：relevant 更日常，pertinent 更正式，带一点「一语中的」的意味。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow that lands exactly in the middle of the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭正落在靶心中央。

abstract.en: Think of a single sentence that solves a long debate.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话就终结了冗长的争论。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand placing one useful file on the table and taking the rest away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在桌上放下一份有用的文件，把其余的都收走。

examples.en: Please keep your comments pertinent to the topic.
examples.cn: 请让评论紧扣主题。

examples.en: The report contains points pertinent to our decision.
examples.cn: 报告中有些要点与我们的决定相关。

examples.en: His pertinent remark saved the team much time.
examples.cn: 他那句中肯的话给团队省了很多时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍提呢」——一拍桌子、一提要点，句句都切题；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（彻底）+ tenere（握住）→ pertinere（伸向、触及、属于）→ pertinens（属于某事的）→ 英语 pertinent，核心义「伸向并属于要点」。

sensesIntro.en: Pertinent starts with belonging to the topic, then means mattering for the problem, and finally praises words that stay on the point.
sensesIntro.cn: pertinent 先指属于话题，再指对问题重要，最后用来称赞不跑题、切中要害的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow that lands exactly in the centre of the matter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭不偏不倚，正好落在讨论的正中。

branches.en: Belonging to the topic gives the plain related sense.
branches.cn: 属于话题给出最普通的「相关」义。

branches.en: Belonging to the problem also makes the point useful.
branches.cn: 属于问题本身也让这一点变得有用。

branches.en: Reaching the point turns into praise for brief, exact speech.
branches.cn: 伸到要点上，转成对简短中肯表达的称赞。

branches.en: A pertinent question is both related and sharply focused.
branches.cn: 切题的问题既相关又焦点集中。

branches.en: Useful and to the point are two sides of the same judgment.
branches.cn: 「有用」与「中肯」是同一判断的两面。

intro.en: Pertinent is built from the Latin prefix per-, the root ten-, and the adjective ending -ent.
intro.cn: pertinent 由拉丁语前缀 per-、词根 ten- 与形容词词尾 -ent 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere means to hold, and per- means thoroughly, so pertinere means to reach or belong.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere 意为握住，per- 意为彻底，pertinere 即伸向、属于。

items.example: The prefix per- intensifies the verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 per- 加强动词的力度。

items.example: The root ten- also appears in tenant.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ten- 也出现在 tenant 中。

items.example: Tenere is the holding verb at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: tenere 是这个词中心那个「握住」的动词。

items.example: Pertinere combines the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: pertinere 组合了前缀与词根。

items.example: The suffix -ent forms the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 构成形容词。

items.example: Pertinence names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: pertinence 指这种性质本身。

items.example: The prefix im- forms impertinent.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 构成 impertinent。

items.example: Appertain adds a prefix to the same root.
items.exampleCN: appertain 在同一词根上前加前缀。

items.example: Contain shows the plain holding meaning of the root.
items.exampleCN: contain 展示词根最朴素的「握住」义。

definition_zh: 普遍的；弥漫的；渗透的
definition_en: spreading through every part of a place, a group, or a situation
core_image: 雾从每个缝隙涌进房间，把每一处都填满
scene: 考试前，学生们在走廊里反复讨论分数，焦虑的情绪传遍整个班级。A pervasive sense of anxiety spread through the exam hall.
sceneCN: 这里 pervasive 是「弥漫的、普遍的」（第 1 个义项：弥漫到每个角落的）；句意：一种焦虑感弥漫了整个考场。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「普遍性；弥漫程度」
去词尾 -ive 得到的基础动词，义为「弥漫于；渗透」
加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地；渗透地」

senses.title: Spread through a whole place
senses.definition: present or noticed in every part of a place or situation
senses.definitionCN: 在一个地方或情境的每个部分都存在或能被察觉
senses.example: A pervasive smell of smoke filled the building.
senses.exampleCN: 整个建筑里弥漫着烟味。
senses.why: The Latin verb pervadere means to pass through, and a sound, smell, or mood that passes through everything fills every corner.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 pervadere 意为「穿过」，声音、气味或情绪穿过所有事物，就会填满每个角落。

senses.title: Found among most people or groups
senses.definition: common in most people, groups, or parts of a system
senses.definitionCN: 在大多数人、群体或系统的大部分中都存在
senses.example: Smartphones have become pervasive in daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 智能手机在日常生活中已经十分普遍。
senses.why: Spreading through a whole group leaves no strong pocket of difference, so the sense widens to what is generally true.
senses.whyCN: 在一整个群体中渗透开来，就不会留下明显不同的角落，于是义项扩大为「普遍如此」。

senses.title: Influencing in a hidden, lasting way
senses.titleCN: 深入渗透的；（影响）无处不在的
senses.definition: having a deep and lasting influence that quietly shapes a system or culture
senses.definitionCN: 产生深远而持久的影响，潜移默化地塑造一个系统或文化
senses.example: The pervasive influence of money shapes many rules.
senses.exampleCN: 金钱那种无所不在的影响塑造了许多规则。
senses.why: Passing through a thing means working inside it, so a pervasive force is one that hides in the details and shapes them.
senses.whyCN: 穿过某物就意味着在它内部起作用，所以 pervasive 的力量会藏在细节里暗中塑造一切。

intro.en: Pervasive comes from Latin pervadere, to pass through, from per-, through, and vadere, to go.
intro.cn: pervasive 来自拉丁语 pervadere（穿过），由 per-（穿过）与 vadere（走）构成。

items.en: Vadere means to go or to walk, and survives in English evade, invade, and pervade.
items.cn: vadere 意为走、行走，英语的 evade、invade、pervade 都保留了它。

items.en: Pervadere means to go through, to spread through, or to penetrate.
items.cn: pervadere 意为穿过、蔓延到、渗透进去。

items.en: Pervasivus appears in later Latin as the adjective of pervadere.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语用 pervadere 的形容词形式表示「穿过的」。

items.en: English pervade arrives first, and pervasive follows as the adjective of spreading through.
items.cn: 英语先出现动词 pervade，随后出现表示「穿透蔓延」的形容词 pervasive。

items.en: Modern English uses pervasive for trends, beliefs, moods, and hidden influences.
items.cn: 现代英语中 pervasive 用于趋势、观念、情绪和隐秘的影响。

note.en: Pervasive shares the Latin going root with invade, evade, and pervade, and stands beside widespread and ubiquitous in meaning.
note.cn: pervasive 与 invade、evade、pervade 共享拉丁语「走」的词根，在意义上靠近 widespread 与 ubiquitous。

entries.definition: to spread through every part of something
the quality of being widespread
to enter by force or in large numbers
to escape or avoid
existing in many places or among many people
seeming to be present everywhere at once
regularly found in a particular place or group

normalIntro.en: Pervasive carries the Latin verb to go through: something that goes through everything is everywhere.
normalIntro.cn: pervasive 带着拉丁语「走过」的意思：穿过一切的东西就无处不在。

normal.en: Pervade is the verb, and pervasive is the adjective made from it.
normal.cn: pervade 是动词，pervasive 是从它变来的形容词。

normal.en: A pervasive problem is one that appears across the whole system and is hard to escape.
normal.cn: pervasive problem 是指遍布整个系统、很难避开的普遍问题。

normal.en: Per- means through, and the root vad- means to go, so per-walking is what pervades.
normal.cn: per- 表示穿过，词根 vad- 表示走，所以「走过去」就是 pervades。

normal.en: Compare invaded: both words contain the Latin word for going in, but one goes in and the other goes through.
normal.cn: 对比 invade：两词都含「走进」的词根，一个走进去，一个穿过去。

normal.en: Pervasiveness is the noun used for how far something reaches, as in the pervasiveness of social media.
normal.cn: pervasiveness 是名词，用来衡量波及的范围，如社交媒体的普遍程度。

abstract.en: Picture fog pushing in through every crack of a room.
abstract.cn: 想象浓雾从房间的每道缝隙里涌进来。

abstract.en: Imagine a rumour that reaches every classroom before lunch.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传言午饭前就传遍每间教室。

abstract.en: Think of a root system secretly running under a whole field.
abstract.cn: 想象根系在整片田野下面悄悄蔓延。

examples.en: A pervasive sense of trust grew in the community.
examples.cn: 社区里逐渐形成了一种普遍的信任感。

examples.en: The pervasive influence of advertising reaches every age group.
examples.cn: 广告那种无所不在的影响遍及各个年龄层。

examples.en: Online sales have become pervasive in recent years.
examples.cn: 近年来网上销售已经变得十分普遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼为势」——水泼出去，收不住势头，弥漫得到处都是；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 per-（穿过）+ vadere（走）→ pervadere（穿过、蔓延）→ pervadere 未完成分词 pervadens（穿过的）→ 英语 pervade 与 pervasive，核心义「走过来、渗透一切」。

sensesIntro.en: Pervasive begins with what fills every part of a place, widens to what most people or systems share, and ends with hidden lasting influence.
sensesIntro.cn: pervasive 先指填满某一处每个部分的，再扩大到大多数人或系统共有的，最后指隐秘而持久的影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fog that flows in through every crack and fills the room.
core.cn: 核心意象：雾从每个缝隙涌进房间，把每一处都填满。

branches.en: Filling every part of a place is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 填满一个地方的每个部分，是基本的义项。

branches.en: Reaching everyone turns into the sense of being common.
branches.cn: 波及所有人，转成「普遍存在」的义项。

branches.en: Working inside the details produces the sense of hidden influence.
branches.cn: 在细节内部起作用，产生「隐蔽影响」的义项。

branches.en: Something that fills every corner is naturally shared by all.
branches.cn: 填满每个角落的东西自然会为所有人共有。

branches.en: A widespread force is also one that quietly shapes behaviour.
branches.cn: 广泛存在的力量也往往在暗中塑造行为。

intro.en: Pervasive is built from the Latin prefix per-, the going root vad-, and the adjective ending -ive.
intro.cn: pervasive 由拉丁语前缀 per-、表示「走」的词根 vad- 与形容词词尾 -ive 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vadere means to go, and per- means through, so pervadere means to go through.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vadere 意为走，per- 意为穿过，pervadere 即走过去、穿过。

items.example: The prefix per- marks movement through.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 per- 标记「穿过」的运动方向。

items.example: The root vad- also appears in invade and evade.
items.exampleCN: 词根 vad- 也出现在 invade 与 evade 中。

items.example: Vadere is the going verb behind the word.
items.exampleCN: vadere 是这个词背后的「走」。

items.meaning: to go through, to spread through
items.example: Pervadere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: pervadere 把前缀与词根连接起来。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms pervasive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 pervasive。

items.example: Pervade is the verb base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: pervade 是这个形容词的动词基础。

items.example: Pervasiveness adds a noun ending to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: pervasiveness 在形容词后加名词词尾。

items.example: The prefix trans- appears in words built on the same root.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 trans- 出现在同一词根构成的词中。

items.example: Invade shows the root with an inward prefix.
items.exampleCN: invade 展示词根加上「向内」的前缀。

definition_zh: 害虫；有害生物；疫病；讨厌的人
definition_en: an insect or small animal that damages crops, food or health, or a person who is a nuisance
core_image: 一只小虫啃穿谷仓的麻袋，谷粒从破口漏成一堆
scene: 田里的幼苗接连枯黄，扒开土层一看，根须被小虫咬断。The farmer found that the pest had eaten the roots of the young rice.
sceneCN: 这里 pest 是「害虫、有害生物」（第 1 个义项：啃食作物、粮食或损害健康的昆虫与小动物）；句意为农夫发现害虫把稻苗的根啃坏了。

derivatives.zh: pest + 拉丁 caedere「杀」的名词形式 -cide，义为「杀虫剂」
与 pest 同源，指「瘟疫；时疫」
由 pest 加动词后缀 -er 构成，义为「不断烦扰；纠缠」
拉丁 pestifer 加 -ous，义为「传播瘟疫的；有害的」

senses.title: A harmful insect or small animal
senses.definition: an insect or small animal that damages crops, stored food or health
senses.definitionCN: 啃食作物、糟蹋储粮或危害健康的昆虫与小动物
senses.example: The tomatoes were ruined by a common garden pest.
senses.exampleCN: 西红柿被一种常见的园中害虫毁了。
senses.why: Latin pestis named a plague or a destructive force, and the word keeps that destructive core: anything that eats or spoils what people need.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pestis 指瘟疫或毁坏性的力量，这个词保留了「毁坏」的核心：凡是啃食或糟蹋人们所需之物的生物，都称得上 pest。

senses.title: A plague or epidemic disease
senses.definition: a deadly infectious disease, or the outbreak of one, as in older uses of the word
senses.definitionCN: 致命传染病，或这类疾病的暴发，多用于较早的用法
senses.example: In old accounts, the pest swept through the city in one summer.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时记载里，那场瘟疫在一个夏天席卷了全城。
senses.why: This was the first meaning of pest: pestis meant plague, and the sickness sense lingered in compounds such as pestilence.
senses.whyCN: 这是 pest 最早的意思：pestis 本义就是瘟疫，疾病义后来保留在 pestilence 这类词里。

senses.title: An annoying person
senses.definition: a person, especially a child, who keeps annoying others
senses.definitionCN: 不断烦扰别人的家伙，多指小孩子
senses.example: Stop being such a pest and let your sister read.
senses.exampleCN: 别这么讨厌，让你姐姐看书。
senses.why: Something that constantly nibbles and spoils things becomes a picture for a person who keeps pestering, so pest also names a nuisance.
senses.whyCN: 不断啃咬、糟蹋东西的生物，正好可以用来形容一个反复纠缠的人，于是 pest 也指让人厌烦的家伙。

senses.title: A troublesome thing or situation
senses.definition: a thing or persistent problem that causes trouble
senses.definitionCN: 带来麻烦的事物或反复出现的问题
senses.example: Flies were a real pest during the picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 野餐时苍蝇真叫人心烦。
senses.why: When the nuisance is a thing rather than a creature, the same sense of spoiling the day carries over to everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 当烦人的对象不是生物而是一件事时，那种「搅坏了兴致」的感觉在日常说法里原样保留下来。

intro.en: Pest comes from Latin pestis, plague or destruction, through Old French peste.
intro.cn: pest 来自拉丁语 pestis（瘟疫、毁灭），经古法语 peste 进入英语。

items.en: The Latin root is generally compared with words for breaking or crumbling, but the reconstructed form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁词根可与表示「折断、碎裂」的词相比较，但重构形式并不确定。

items.en: Pestis means a plague, a plague or destruction, and pestilentia names pestilence.
items.cn: pestis 意为瘟疫、毁灭，pestilentia 指瘟疫。

items.en: Pestifer combines pestis with ferre, to carry, for plague bearing.
items.cn: pestifer 把 pestis 与 ferre（携带）组合，表示「带疫的」。

items.en: Peste carries the word into French with the plague sense.
items.cn: peste 把这个词连同瘟疫义带入法语。

items.en: Pest first names the plague, then any animal that damages crops or food.
items.cn: 英语里的 pest 先指瘟疫，后扩展到损害作物或粮食的动物。

items.en: Pest control and pesticides make the word central to farming and everyday annoyance.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pest control 与 pesticide 把 pest 推到农业和日常烦恼的中心。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin pestis; the near-meaning group gathers creatures and people treated as troublesome.
note.cn: 形近组收同出拉丁语 pestis 的一族词；近义组收被当作祸害的生物与人物。

entries.definition: a deadly infectious disease
to annoy someone repeatedly
a chemical used to kill pests
a small creature with six legs and a body in three parts
entries.definitionCN: 昆虫（只是类别词，不一定有害）

entries.definition: small animals such as rats and insects that cause harm
entries.definitionCN: 害兽；害虫（多指老鼠等，单复同形）

entries.definition: a person or thing that annoys others

normalIntro.en: Pest keeps the plague idea at its root and widens to crops, food and people.
normalIntro.cn: pest 的词根保存着「瘟疫」的观念，并扩展到作物、粮食与人。

normal.en: Pest control companies spray fields to keep insects away.
normal.cn: pest control 指害虫防治，农户会喷药把虫子赶走。

normal.en: Pestilence is the old plague word from the same Latin pestis.
normal.cn: pestilence 是古老的瘟疫词，同样来自拉丁语 pestis。

normal.en: To pester someone is to act like a pest toward them.
normal.cn: pester 某人就是对他像 pest 一样纠缠不停。

normal.en: Pesticide joins pest and the Latin root for killing.
normal.cn: pesticide 由 pest 加上拉丁语「杀」的词根构成。

normal.en: Compare insect: an insect is any six-legged creature, a pest only one that harms.
normal.cn: 对比 insect：insect 泛指六条腿的昆虫，pest 只指有害的那类。

abstract.en: Picture a weevil chewing a hole in a sack of grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一只象鼻虫在粮袋上啃出一个洞。

abstract.en: Imagine a medieval town with a warning bell for the plague.
abstract.cn: 想象中世纪的城镇，瘟疫来临时敲响警钟。

abstract.en: See a child hopping around a table while everyone is trying to work.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子在桌边跳来跳去，大家却都要工作。

examples.en: Farmers use fewer chemicals to control pests in the field.
examples.cn: 农民用更少的农药来控制田里的害虫。

examples.en: Stored grain can be destroyed by pests such as weevils and mice.
examples.cn: 储存的粮食会被象鼻虫、老鼠这类害虫毁掉。

examples.en: My little brother can be a real pest when he wants attention.
examples.cn: 我弟弟想引起注意的时候真能烦人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍死它」——一见就拍，正合害虫 pest 的本义；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pestis（瘟疫、毁灭）→ 古法语 peste → 英语 pest，核心义「带来毁坏之物」；pestilence、pestiferous、pesticide 均出自同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Pest starts with the plague, moves to creatures that spoil crops and food, and finally to annoying people and things.
sensesIntro.cn: pest 先指瘟疫，再指糟蹋作物与粮食的生物，最后引申为烦人的人与事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small insect chews a hole in a grain sack.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小虫把粮袋啃出一个洞。

branches.en: The creature sense is the most common today: pests eat crops and stored food.
branches.cn: 生物义是今天最常用的：pest 啃食作物与储粮。

branches.en: The plague sense is the oldest and survives in older writing and compounds.
branches.cn: 瘟疫义最古老，保留在较早的文献与复合词中。

branches.en: A person who keeps bothering others takes over the nuisance sense.
branches.cn: 反复纠缠他人的人继承了「烦人」这一层。

branches.en: A thing that spoils the moment, such as clouds of flies, is called a pest too.
branches.cn: 搅坏兴致的事物，比如成群的苍蝇，也叫 pest。

branches.en: Both a crop pest and the plague are forces that destroy what a community depends on.
branches.cn: 作物害虫与瘟疫都是摧毁社群赖以生存之物的力量。

intro.en: Pest is a Latin noun that grows compounds and derivatives in English with pesti- as the linking form.
intro.cn: pest 是拉丁语名词，在英语里以 pesti- 为连接形式生出复合词与派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pestis gives pest, pestilentia and pestifer, and the later compounds keep the shortened stem pesti-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pestis 生出 pest、pestilentia 与 pestifer，后来的复合词沿用缩短的词干 pesti-。

items.example: Pest is the short everyday form.
items.exampleCN: pest 是日常使用的短形式。

items.example: The stem pesti- links the Latin compounds.
items.exampleCN: 词干 pesti- 把拉丁复合词连在一起。

items.example: The suffix -cide makes pesticide.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cide 构成 pesticide。

items.example: Pesticide names a chemical killer of pests.
items.exampleCN: pesticide 指杀灭害虫的化学药剂。

items.meaning: a person who does an action
items.example: The suffix -er forms pester from pest.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 由 pest 构成 pester。

items.example: Pestilence adds -ence to the plague stem.
items.exampleCN: pestilence 在瘟疫词干后加 -ence。

items.example: Pestiferous is built with -ferous.
items.exampleCN: pestiferous 用 -ferous 构成。

items.example: Pest control is the common compound phrase.
items.exampleCN: pest control 是常见复合短语。

latinEntries.structure: Latin adjective from pestis and ferre

definition_zh: 杀虫剂；农药
definition_en: a chemical substance used to kill insects, weeds or other organisms that harm crops
core_image: 烟囱一样的喷头喷出药雾，落在沾满小虫的菜叶上
scene: 果园里的果子还没熟，就被虫子咬出一个个洞，果农只得在枝头喷药。The orchard keeper sprayed pesticide on the trees to stop the insects.
sceneCN: 这里 pesticide 是「杀虫剂、农药」（第 1 个义项：用来杀死危害作物生物的化学药剂）；句意为果农在树上喷洒农药来止住虫害。

derivatives.zh: pesticide 的第一部分，义为「害虫；有害生物」
pest 加 control，义为「害虫防治」
与 pest 同源，义为「瘟疫」
herbi-「草」加 -cide「杀」，属同一类农药词

senses.title: A chemical for killing pests
senses.definition: a chemical used to kill insects or other organisms that harm crops or stored food
senses.definitionCN: 用来杀灭危害作物或储粮的昆虫等生物的化学药剂
senses.example: The farmer sprayed a pesticide over the cabbages.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫在卷心菜上喷了杀虫剂。
senses.why: Latin pestis is a pest or plague, and the suffix -cide means a killing, so a pesticide is literally a plague killer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pestis 是害虫、瘟疫，后缀 -cide 意为「杀」，所以 pesticide 字面就是「杀瘟除虫之物」。

senses.title: A pesticide in the broad sense
senses.definition: any product for plant protection, including herbicides, fungicides and insecticides
senses.definitionCN: 泛指一切用于保护作物的药剂，包括除草剂、杀菌剂和杀虫剂
senses.example: Regulators treat herbicides and insecticides as forms of pesticide.
senses.exampleCN: 监管部门把除草剂和杀虫剂都归为农药。
senses.why: Because pest was widened to any harmful organism, modern English uses pesticide as the umbrella word for farm chemicals.
senses.whyCN: 因为 pest 早已扩展到泛指各种有害生物，现代英语便用 pesticide 作各类农药的总称。

senses.title: Residue left on food or in the environment
senses.definition: the chemical trace left on food or in soil and water after spraying
senses.definitionCN: 喷洒后残留在食物上，或留在土壤和水里的药物
senses.example: The lab tests fruit for pesticide residue.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室检测水果中的农药残留。
senses.why: A name for the product easily comes to stand for what it leaves behind, so pesticide also points to traces and pollution.
senses.whyCN: 产品的名称很容易转指它留下的东西，于是 pesticide 也用来指残留与污染。

intro.en: Pesticide is a coined compound: Latin pestis plus the suffix -cide from Latin caedere, to cut down or kill.
intro.cn: pesticide 是人工造出的复合词：拉丁语 pestis 加上来自 caedere（砍倒、杀死）的后缀 -cide。

items.en: Pestis means plague or destruction, the base of pest.
items.cn: pestis 意为瘟疫或毁灭，是 pest 的词基。

items.en: Caedere means to cut down or slaughter, giving the suffix -cide.
items.cn: caedere 意为砍倒、宰杀，衍生出后缀 -cide。

items.en: The word pesticide is coined in the late nineteenth century, following older -cide words such as homicide and insecticide.
items.cn: pesticide 在十九世纪后期被造出，仿照 homicide、insecticide 这类更早的 -cide 词。

items.en: The word rises with industrial crop chemicals and their regulation.
items.cn: 随着工业化农用化学品及其监管的出现，这个词流行起来。

items.en: Pesticide becomes the umbrella term, with insecticide and herbicide as more specific words.
items.cn: 现代英语中 pesticide 成了总称，insecticide 与 herbicide 则是更具体的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers -cide words that share the killing suffix; the near-meaning group gathers farm chemicals with narrower targets.
note.cn: 形近组收共用「杀」后缀的 -cide 词；近义组收针对目标更具体的农用药剂。

entries.definition: a substance that kills insects
a substance that kills plants
the act of killing oneself
entries.definitionCN: 自杀（后缀 -cide 同源，指杀）

entries.definition: a substance that kills fungi
a substance added to soil to help plants grow
entries.definitionCN: 肥料（作用是滋养，不是杀灭）

entries.definition: a substance that harms living things

normalIntro.en: Pesticide is built from two Latin pieces and sits in a whole family of -cide words.
normalIntro.cn: pesticide 由两块拉丁成分构成，并和一大群 -cide 词同族。

normal.en: Pest means a harmful creature, so pesticide kills pests.
normal.cn: pest 指有害生物，所以 pesticide 就是杀灭它们的药剂。

normal.en: The suffix -cide appears in homicide, suicide and genocide, all about killing.
normal.cn: 后缀 -cide 出现在 homicide、suicide、genocide 里，都跟「杀」有关。

normal.en: Fertilizer feeds plants, while pesticide kills what feeds on them.
normal.cn: fertilizer 是给植物吃的，pesticide 是杀吃植物的东西。

normal.en: Ordinary spraying uses pesticides in the plural.
normal.cn: 日常说喷洒的时候，pesticides 常用复数。

normal.en: Compare insecticide: it targets insects only, not every pest.
normal.cn: 对比 insecticide：它只针对昆虫，并非所有 pest。

abstract.en: Picture a fine cloud of spray settling on a half-eaten leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象一片细密的药雾落在被啃掉一半的叶子上。

abstract.en: See the word split in two: pest and cide, a killer of creatures.
abstract.cn: 把这个词一劈两半：pest 加 cide，就是「杀生物者」。

abstract.en: Imagine a supermarket label warning about pesticide traces.
abstract.cn: 想象超市标签上写着农药残留的警示。

examples.en: Many farms now use fewer pesticides to protect water supplies.
examples.cn: 如今许多农场减少使用农药，以保护水源。

examples.en: Pesticide residue on vegetables worries some consumers.
examples.cn: 蔬菜上的农药残留让一些消费者担忧。

examples.en: Overuse of pesticide can harm bees and other useful insects.
examples.cn: 过量使用杀虫剂会伤害蜜蜂和其他益虫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍死它戴」——拍死它，再给它戴一顶喷药的帽子，就是杀虫剂；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pestis（害虫、瘟疫）+ 拉丁 caedere（砍倒、杀死）的后缀形式 -cide → 英语 pesticide，核心义「杀灭害虫之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Pesticide first names an insect killer, widens to all crop chemicals, and finally stands for what the chemical leaves behind.
sensesIntro.cn: pesticide 先指杀灭虫子的药剂，再扩展为各类作物用药，最后转指药剂留下的痕迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sprayer sends a fine cloud of chemicals over a leaf covered with insects.
core.cn: 核心意象：喷头把细密的药雾洒满爬着虫子的叶片。

branches.en: The everyday sense is the bottle that kills crop pests.
branches.cn: 日常义就是那瓶能杀死作物害虫的药剂。

branches.en: The umbrella sense covers herbicides and fungicides as well.
branches.cn: 总称义把除草剂与杀菌剂也一并涵盖。

branches.en: The trace sense names what is left on food, soil and water.
branches.cn: 残留义指食物、土壤与水中留下的药物。

branches.en: Both use the same killing root, just with a narrower or wider target list.
branches.cn: 两者共用同一个「杀」词根，只是目标范围一窄一宽。

branches.en: The product and its residue are spoken of with one word in public debate.
branches.cn: 公共讨论里常用一个词同时指产品与它的残留。

intro.en: Pesticide is a two-part compound, and each part also appears in other English words.
intro.cn: pesticide 是两部分组成的复合词，每一部分也出现在别的英语词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin pestis provides the first element, while -cide goes back to caedere, to cut down.
latinIntro.cn: 第一部分来自拉丁语 pestis，后缀 -cide 则源自 caedere（砍倒、杀）。

items.example: The first element pest- comes from pestis.
items.exampleCN: 第一部分 pest- 来自 pestis。

items.example: The suffix -cide makes insecticide.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cide 构成 insecticide。

items.example: Insecticide targets insects in particular.
items.exampleCN: insecticide 专门针对昆虫。

items.example: Herbicide uses herba, a plant.
items.exampleCN: herbicide 用 herba（草）作词干。

items.example: Fungicide follows the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: fungicide 沿用同一构词方式。

items.example: Pest is the short base word.
items.exampleCN: pest 是简短的基础词。

items.example: Pest control may use chemicals or traps.
items.exampleCN: pest control 可以用药剂或陷阱。

items.meaning: a broad-range killer of living things
items.example: Biocide is the widest of the family.
items.exampleCN: biocide 是这一族里范围最宽的词。

definition_zh: 花瓣；花瓣状物
definition_en: one of the coloured, leaf-like parts that form the flower around its centre
core_image: 一朵花在桌面上摊开，一片片薄而软的花瓣围成一圈
scene: 桌上放着一朵刚摘下的玫瑰，风一吹，最外侧的花瓣先飘了下来。She pressed a pink petal between the pages of her notebook.
sceneCN: 这里 petal 是「花瓣」（第 1 个义项：花冠上薄而带颜色的一片）；句意为她把一片粉红的花瓣夹在笔记本里。

derivatives.zh: petal 加 -ed，义为「有……花瓣的」，多用于复合词
petal 加希腊语词缀 -oid「像」，义为「花瓣状的」
petal 加 -ous，义为「有花瓣的；花瓣状的」
前缀 a-「无」加 petalous，义为「无花瓣的」

senses.title: One coloured part of a flower
senses.definition: one of the usually coloured, leaf-like parts that surround the centre of a flower
senses.definitionCN: 围在花心周围、通常带颜色的叶状薄片
senses.example: Each petal of the lily curls back at the tip.
senses.exampleCN: 百合的每片花瓣顶端都向后卷起。
senses.why: Greek petalon meant a thin leaf or plate, so the nearest leaf-like plate of a flower became its petal.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 petalon 指薄叶或薄片，所以花朵上最贴近叶子的那层薄片，就叫做花瓣。

senses.title: A petal considered as a plant organ
senses.definition: a sterile floral part, often in a whorl called the corolla, that attracts pollinators
senses.definitionCN: 植物学上指不育的叶片状器官，常组成花冠以吸引传粉者
senses.example: In botany a petal is a modified leaf that belongs to the corolla.
senses.exampleCN: 在植物学里，花瓣是构成花冠的变态叶。
senses.why: Plant biology inherited the word and gave it a precise place among the sterile flower organs.
senses.whyCN: 植物学沿用了这个词，并把它安放在花器中不育器官的精确位置上。

senses.title: A petal shape in designs and compounds
senses.definition: a thin curved shape like a petal, or the element petal used in compound words
senses.definitionCN: 形状像花瓣的薄片，或作为构词成分的 petal
senses.example: The lamp has a large, petal-shaped shade.
senses.exampleCN: 这盏灯有一个较大的花瓣形灯罩。
senses.why: Because a petal is a clear rounded plate, its shape and its combining form carry over to glass, design and technical compounds.
senses.whyCN: 花瓣是一片清晰的弧形薄片，因此它的形状和构词形式被沿用到玻璃、设计与技术复合词中。

intro.en: Petal comes from Greek petalon, a leaf or a thin plate, through modern Latin.
intro.cn: petal 来自希腊语 petalon（叶、薄片），经由近代拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Greek petalon is generally derived from a root meaning to spread out flat, in reconstructed form.
items.cn: 一般认为希腊语 petalon 来自表示「铺平、展开」的词根，但这只是重构形式。

items.en: Petalon means a leaf, a leaf of a plant, or a flat plate.
items.cn: petalon 意为叶子、植物的叶，或平坦的薄片。

items.en: The Latin writers left petalon largely to Greek botany.
items.cn: 拉丁语作家大多把这个词留给希腊植物学使用。

items.en: Botanists adopt petalum for a flower leaf, and English petal follows.
items.cn: 十八世纪的植物学家用 petalum 指花瓣，英语 petal 随之而来。

items.en: Petal enters English as a plant term and spreads to everyday use.
items.cn: petal 作为植物学词汇进入英语，后扩展到日常用法。

items.en: Petal now also means a petal-shaped thing and a combining element.
items.cn: 现代英语里 petal 还指花瓣状之物，并作构词成分使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers flower parts and related plant words; the near-meaning group gathers petals and petal-like pieces in other fields.
note.cn: 形近组收花器各部位与相关植物词；近义组收花瓣以及其他领域里形似花瓣的片状物。

entries.definition: a leaf-like part under the petals
entries.definitionCN: 萼片（包在花瓣外面的绿色小片）

entries.definition: a lever worked by the foot
entries.definitionCN: 踏板；只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自 foot）

entries.definition: the stalk of a leaf
entries.definitionCN: 叶柄（与 petal 同出拉丁 petiolus）

entries.definition: a flower, especially on a fruit tree
a flower, or the state of flowering
a small thin flat piece
entries.definitionCN: 薄片（与花瓣同为薄而平的小片）

normalIntro.en: Petal goes back to the Greek word for a leaf, and its relatives stay in the same plant family.
normalIntro.cn: petal 上溯到希腊语里表示「叶」的词，它的同族词也都在植物范畴里。

normal.en: Petal and sepal name two neighbouring rings of a flower.
normal.cn: petal 与 sepal 分别指花朵相邻的两圈结构。

normal.en: Petal ends in -al, while pedal ends in -d like foot.
normal.cn: petal 以 -al 结尾，pedal 以 -d 结尾，像脚一样踩在踏板上。

normal.en: Petal is related to petiole, the leaf stalk.
normal.cn: petal 与表示叶柄的 petiole 同源。

normal.en: Prefix a- negates it: apetalous means without petals.
normal.cn: 前缀 a- 表示否定：apetalous 即「无花瓣的」。

normal.en: Compare petal and petal-like: the shape is borrowed in many compounds.
normal.cn: 对比 petal 与 petal-like：这个词的形状义被许多复合词借用。

abstract.en: Picture a fallen petal resting on an open book.
abstract.cn: 想象一片落下的花瓣停在摊开的书页上。

abstract.en: See a ring of petals turning toward the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈花瓣朝着太阳的方向。

abstract.en: Think of a lampshade cut into several rounded lobes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被切成几瓣弧形的灯罩。

examples.en: White petals covered the ground after the wind.
examples.cn: 起风之后，白色花瓣铺了一地。

examples.en: The teacher asked us to count the petals on each flower.
examples.cn: 老师让我们数一数每朵花上有几片花瓣。

examples.en: Candied rose petal is used to decorate the cake.
examples.cn: 糖渍玫瑰花瓣被用来装饰蛋糕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派头」——花开得最有派头的时候，就是花瓣一圈圈围起来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 petalon（叶、薄片）→ 拉丁 petalum → 英语 petal；同族词 petiole「叶柄」，核心义「花朵上最像叶子的一层薄片」。

sensesIntro.en: Petal starts as one coloured leaf-like part of a flower, then becomes a botanical organ, then a shape and a combining element.
sensesIntro.cn: petal 先指花朵上一片带颜色的叶状薄片，再成为植物学器官，最后成为形状与构词成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft thin petals lie in a ring around the heart of a flower.
core.cn: 核心意象：柔软的花瓣围成一圈，托住花心。

branches.en: The everyday sense is one coloured piece of a flower.
branches.cn: 日常义就是花朵上一片带颜色的薄片。

branches.en: Botany fixes its place in the corolla and its role in attracting pollinators.
branches.cn: 植物学把它固定在花冠里，并定义它吸引传粉者的作用。

branches.en: Its rounded plate shape moves into design, glass and compounds.
branches.cn: 它弧形的薄片形状进入设计、玻璃与复合词。

branches.en: The ordinary petal is simply the botanical organ seen without a microscope.
branches.cn: 日常所说的花瓣，就是不用显微镜去看的那个植物学器官。

branches.en: A petal-shaped object borrows the outline, not the plant itself.
branches.cn: 花瓣状物体借用的是外形轮廓，而不是植物本身。

intro.en: Petal itself is a Greek noun, and English builds adjectives and compounds around it with -ed, -oid and a-.
intro.cn: petal 本身是希腊语名词，英语围绕它用 -ed、-oid、a- 等成分构成形容词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Greek petalon, passed on as Latin petalum; the Latin relatives petiolus and petalum keep the leaf idea.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是希腊语 petalon，转写为拉丁 petalum；拉丁同族词 petiolus 与 petalum 都保留「叶片」之意。

items.example: Petalon is the Greek source of petal.
items.exampleCN: petalon 是 petal 的希腊语来源。

items.meaning: one coloured part of a flower
items.example: Petal is the base word of the family.
items.exampleCN: petal 是这一词族的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms petalled.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 petalled。

items.example: Petalled is used in compound adjectives.
items.exampleCN: petalled 多用于复合形容词。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms petaloid.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -oid 构成 petaloid。

items.example: The prefix a- forms apetalous.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 a- 构成 apetalous。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms petalous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 petalous。

items.example: Petiole is the leaf-stalk cousin of petal.
items.exampleCN: petiole 是与 petal 同源的表叶柄词。

items.meaning: one of the outer green parts of a flower
